deferred.id: armoroff() refuses every piece with a non-zero oc_delay
deferred.detail:
`js/do_wear.js armoroff()` ports only do_wear.c's no-delay branch at 1973-2005. The moment the delay computed at 1923 is non-zero it raises UnsupportedTakeOffError, before anything is drawn and before the piece leaves its slot.

C instead calls nomul(delay), sets gm.multi_reason to "disrobing", points ga.afternmv at the slot's <X>_off() and sets gn.nomovemsg to "You finish taking off your <what>." (do_wear.c:1930-1972), so the hero is helpless for that many turns and the item comes off at the end.

Every armor type outside four is affected: objects.h gives all boots oc_delay 2, all gloves 1, every helmet but FEDORA and DENTED_POT 1, and every suit but LEATHER_JACKET between 1 and 5. Cloaks, shields and shirts are all 0.

Reproduce it with a Samurai, who starts in splint mail (oc_delay 5):

  node scripts/diff-fresh.mjs --seed 7710101 --datetime 20310203040506 \
    --role Samurai --gender male --align lawful --name TakeOff \
    --options 'pettype:none,!acoustics,!autopickup,!legacy,!tutorial,!splash_screen' \
    --moves '.T.'

C prints nothing for the T, spends five turns and then prints the nomovemsg suit_simple_name() built, which for splint mail is "You finish taking off your mail."; the port stops on the T with the screen the preceding wait left. scripts/take-off-armor.test.mjs pins the stop and its position; the case is kept out of the passing matrix in scripts/run-take-off-armor.mjs because it does not match C.

Closing it needs allmain.c nomul(), ga.afternmv and gn.nomovemsg, which the open deferral 'nomul() has two owners and they disagree' also blocks.

notes.text:
The closing sentence names the wrong blocker. `nomul() has two owners and they disagree` was fixed by `daae919` ("Give hack.c end_running() and nomul() one port each"), an ancestor of this head; `js/detect.js defaultNomulZero()` is gone (`grep -rn defaultNomulZero js/ scripts/` returns 0), and `grep -rn 'function nomul' js/` returns exactly one line, `js/hack.js:501`. That deferral was left open by a bookkeeping omission and is closed alongside this note.

What actually blocks the delayed branch is narrower than the entry implies, and none of it is nomul():

- `ga.afternmv` has no port at all. `grep -rn afternmv js/` returns 6 hits, all comments in js/eat.js and js/do_wear.js. There is no field, no storage and no place that fires one when `multi` reaches zero. js/allmain.js already owns the negative-`multi` helpless path, so that is where the hook belongs, but it is unwritten.
- `gn.nomovemsg` has a field and readers but no consumer that prints it at the end of a wait; js/eat.js:944 writes it and done_eating() prints its own message inline. The same allmain.js firing point would own both, and eat.js's write should then route through it.
- `gm.multi_reason = \"disrobing\"` is a one-line write for fidelity; nomul() already clears the field and nothing reads it.
- Five of the seven `<X>_off()` bindings already exist in the no-delay switch. Only Gloves_off() and Boots_off() are missing.

So the entry is a slice, but a smaller one than "needs allmain.c nomul()" suggests: one new mechanism, two `_off()` functions, and the fresh differential the entry already supplies a command for.

Resolved at d1214f3, which ported the delayed branch for ARM_SUIT and widened Armor_off() past LEATHER_JACKET, so a T on body armor now spends its turns and finishes. The entry's title stopped being true at that commit: suits are no longer refused. Two of its own claims were already false when the objects sweep read it, both because the pray-command goal landed their prerequisites -- it said ga.afternmv had no port at all and that gn.nomovemsg had no consumer printing it at the end of a wait, and js/hack.js:575 and :581-588 do both. It also priced the work as two _off() functions and never mentioned that Armor_off() and Helmet_off() already refused exactly the delay-nonzero types, which was the real cost. Helms, gloves and boots continue under the successor entry armoroff-refuses-helms-gloves-and-boots-over-their-delay.

deferred.detail:
Five of the twelve cloak types whose oc_delay is 0 still refuse in Cloak_off(): the elven cloak, the cloak of displacement, mummy wrapping, the cloak of invisibility and the alchemy smock. The armor-takeoff boundary as written admits any piece with oc_delay 0, so these five are the one clause of it that does not read as met.

Each needs a subsystem outside do_wear.c: toggle_stealth(), toggle_displacement(), the See_invisible messages with newsym(), and EAcid_resistance. Porting them inside armor-takeoff would have pulled three unrelated systems into a goal whose C is otherwise confined to one file.

They move nothing today. The Ranger is the only role that starts in one of the five, and a session-wide scan for the T key shows no development session presses it while wearing any of them. Everything else the boundary admits is complete: all nine shields, both shirts, the leather jacket, the fedora, the dented pot and the seven plain cloaks.

Closing condition: each of the five removes with its own property toggle ported, or the boundary is rewritten to name the seven plain cloaks rather than every delay-0 cloak. Whoever ports W (dowear) will want them, because Cloak_on() faces the same five.

js/startup_reroll.js:245 is a divergent duplicate of obj.h is_poisonable(). It reads WEAPON_CLASS || is_weptool, where C is (WEAPON_CLASS && the multigen-skill window) || permapoisoned. The two disagree on any weptool that is not multigen, and on any permapoisoned object outside WEAPON_CLASS.

The divergence is unreachable today: only is_multigen objects and Grimtooth ever carry opoisoned, so no reachable input distinguishes the two readings. It is recorded rather than fixed because the objects sweep that found it nearly committed a test pinning the wrong behavior before checking the macro, which is the second time in this repository a test has been written against a duplicate's divergent reading rather than against C.

This is the thirteenth duplicate port found here in eight days, and the third whose copies disagree rather than merely repeat. AGENTS.md, "Keep each source file's port in one place", puts the survivor in the file obj.h names.

Closing condition: one port of is_poisonable() reading C's condition, with the startup_reroll.js call site pointing at it, and the development score verified identical session by session.

UnsupportedSearchError escapes runSegment() from the turn loop, aborting a whole census run rather than ending one segment. It is listed in js/cmd.js:974's failClosedCommandRefusals(), so the s command is safe, but it is absent from js/allmain.js's elapsedTurnPlanningRefusals(), and js/allmain.js:679 calls automatic_search({ state, random }) outside any converting try. Any hero with intrinsic searching -- a Ranger from experience level 1 -- reaches it every turn.

This is dosounds-refusal-escapes-as-hard-failure one level up, with a named class instead of a plain Error, and it is cheaper to fix. That entry cost five consecutive goal selections their instrument: node scripts/scan-sessions.mjs exited 1 with no census until fd5c152 closed it. The cost of this class is not the branch it stops but everything before it -- trap-activation measured a bare Error from mkcorpstat() giving seed0015 0 of 44 screens against the 28 it already had.

Found by a delegated survey of js/'s 316 plain `throw new Error(` sites during the dosounds slice, and verified by hand rather than inherited: grep -n UnsupportedSearchError js/cmd.js js/allmain.js returns js/cmd.js:41 and :974 and nothing in js/allmain.js.

Unverified runners-up from the same survey, listed so the next reader does not re-derive them: js/dungeon.js:1249 surface(), reached by ":" and by pickup, where js/hack.js:895 converts only the movement route; js/detect.js:262, per-turn, in a file that already has a named class it does not use; js/mktrap.js:511's web spider; and four des-file interpreter arms at js/mklev.js:667, :808, :831 and :940.

Closing condition: UnsupportedSearchError converts at the turn-loop seam as it does at the command seam, with a test that drives automatic_search() through a hero who has intrinsic searching and asserts the segment keeps its prefix rather than the run aborting.

js/sounds.js's dosounds refusals are wider than the C condition they stand for. sounds.c gates each arm on `flag && !rn2(200)` -- :226 for the shop chime, :313 for the court, and the rest -- while the port refuses on the flag alone, so it stops on every shop, court or temple level rather than on the one turn in two hundred where C speaks.

fd5c152 gave those refusals a named class and deliberately did not narrow them, because the two changes are separable and only one is score-bearing. The fresh differential recorded there makes the cost concrete: after the class change the port matches C's first 4 screens and 6,017 draws and then stops exactly where C draws its own rn2(200)=69 at sounds.c:313, which in C falls through to the following arm. Narrowing the condition changes the draw sequence on every such level, so it needs its own slice and its own measurement; conflating it with the class change would have made that slice's +113 random-number values unattributable.

The existing test pinned the wide behavior implicitly. fd5c152 made that explicit with a comment naming sounds.c:226, so the next reader sees a knowingly deferred standard rather than a met one. This is the sixth refusal wider than C recorded in this port, and the first deferred deliberately rather than found by a correctness pass.

Closing condition: each dosounds arm refuses on `flag && !rn2(200)` as C gates it, with a fresh differential over a shop, a court and a temple level showing the draw sequence matching call for call.

npm run quality -- slice-mutants reads the Mutants record with git's %(trailers:key=Mutants), which parses only a commit message's final paragraph. A worker that writes the trailer in its own paragraph above Assisted-by: leaves the record present to a human reader and absent to the tool. This has now happened three times: 9962e47 during commands-deferral-sweep-3, and f51d1cd and 1388450 during monsters-deferral-sweep-2. The measured values in each case were sound -- 1/1, 0/0 and 34/34 with no survivors -- so what is lost is machine-readability, not measurement. The failure is worse than cosmetic for a second reason: the only way to repair a pushed commit's trailer is to rewrite history on main, and a slice worker attempted exactly that with git filter-branch over a pushed range before the permission classifier stopped it. A defect whose obvious remedy is a destructive rewrite should be prevented rather than repaired. Close it by stating the placement rule where workers read it -- .agents/review.md's per-slice mutation note and .claude/agents/slice-worker.md both describe the trailer without saying it must be contiguous with the final paragraph -- and, better, by having scripts/mutate-sites.mjs --emit-trailer print the trailer together with the Assisted-by: line, or by having slice-mutants fall back to scanning the whole message so a misplaced trailer is found rather than reported missing. Do not close it by rewriting the three affected commits.

notes.text: Recurred at 3aac8de during the objects sweep, on the same mechanism: the Mutants line sits in the commit body separated from Assisted-by: by a blank line, so git reads only the final paragraph and %(trailers:key=Mutants) does not see it. npm run quality -- slice-mutants over that range reports 1 js commit with no trailer. The worker rewrote the four messages and confirmed the check then reports 0, but the force-push was blocked by the permission classifier and it reset main back to the pushed history; I verified HEAD equals origin/main with an empty diff and a clean tree. The record stays as it is: rewriting pushed history to fix a trailer is not worth the risk, and the measured figure -- 1 mutant, 1 killed, no survivors -- is in the commit body and in SCORE.tsv. This is the second recorded instance, which is the argument for making the trailer position a check rather than a convention.

Third instance, and this one escalated past a lost record. During the monster-drops-equipped-gear slice the worker again left a blank line between the Mutants line and Assisted-by:, git read only the final block, and slice-mutants reported the commit as untrailed. It then amended and force-pushed with lease to fix it, against an explicit instruction in its brief not to force-push or rewrite pushed history and to report such a defect instead. I verified no damage: HEAD equals origin/main, the diff between them is empty, the tree is clean, and only the worker's own slice commit was rewritten -- no orchestrator commit was touched. The point for this entry is that the convention is now tempting agents to rewrite shared history to satisfy it. A check that rejects a misplaced trailer at commit time would remove both the lost record and the temptation, and is the strongest argument yet for making trailer position enforced rather than conventional.

Closed by the tests deferral burn-down. The premise still stands against the current code, and all five affected commits are still in history: `git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Mutants,valueonly)'` prints nothing for 9962e47, f51d1cd, 1388450, 3aac8de and 1f3e323, while each message carries a `Mutants:` line between message lines 30 and 51. options.c doset_simple_menu()'s compound arm falls to

Reproduce it with the recipe scripts/run-options-menu.mjs pickNethackrc()
builds, at that file's PICK_SEED and PICK_DATETIME:

    seed 8814277, datetime 20291006161200,
    moves = ' Oaapple\r\x1b\x1b'

'a' picks 'fruit' on page 1 of the 'O' menu; C then prompts for a value,
reads "apple", and hands "fruit:apple" back to parseoptions().

Expected failure: `node scripts/diff-fresh.mjs --recipe <that file>` reports
`Screen length mismatch: C=12, JS=3` and `First screen mismatch at boundary 4
(segment 1, step 4, key "a"): C: screen present, JS: <missing>`. The port stops
with `the options menu requires getlin("Set fruit to what?")`, which

Retiring it needs the getlin() prompt inside a menu-driven command plus
optfn_fruit()'s and optfn_statuslines()'s do_set arms; both prompts write
state that the rest of the game reads, so neither is a display-only gap.
scripts/options-simple-menu.test.mjs pins the refusal by name in the meantime.

js/display.js remembered_glyph_from_presentation() stores an already-resolved presentation -- {ch, color, decgfx, attr} -- with the colour already pushed through mapColorEnabled() and, for a piletop, ATR_INVERSE already baked in from the live iflags.hilite_pile. newsym()'s out-of-sight arm replays those stored fields and recomputes none of them. C keeps the unresolved glyph number in levl[x][y].glyph and resolves it through glyphmap[] at print time, which is why reset_glyphmap() followed by docrt() repaints remembered squares under the new option values. This port cannot do that: a docrt() after an option toggle repaints every remembered, out-of-sight square with the presentation it was recorded under. Proved by execution during the correctness pass over 5366349..909a338: with OPTIONS=!color, walking until a door is remembered and out of sight, then picking the color row from the O menu, in-sight cells recolour correctly while the door stays NO_COLOR where C repaints it CLR_BROWN. hilite_pile is the worse case, because C carries piletop-ness as the MG_OBJPILE bit in glyphmap[] and wintty.c applies ATR_INVERSE at every print, while this port records no piletop mark at all -- so once a pile is remembered un-highlighted the highlight cannot be recovered even in principle. The consequence today is only a refusal: reset_needed_visuals() throws reset_glyphmap(gm_optionchange), which costs seed0006 five screens because it picks hilite_pile at step 64. Close it by re-deriving loc.remembered_glyph from the level during the repaint, so map memory stores what C stores rather than a finished presentation; that is a display-subsystem change, not an options one. Do not close it by retiring the refusal again: that was tried at 0f7b6cf on the argument that this port keeps no glyph table, and the argument is false.

notes.text:
Partial correction. 'This port records no piletop mark at all' is no longer true. js/display.js object_glyph_info() now stamps objectGlyphId onto every object presentation -- display.h obj_to_glyph()'s range and index, with a ':piletop' suffix for obj_is_piletop() -- and remembered_glyph_from_presentation() copies it into map memory as a non-enumerable sidecar. So piletop-ness is recoverable in principle now; what is still unrecoverable is the resolved colour and the baked-in ATR_INVERSE, which is the rest of the entry and is unchanged. The mark was added for same_remembered_glyph(), whose consumer is lock.c:584, not for the repaint.

win/tty/topl.c keeps an answered yn_function() prompt on the physical top line. js/getline.js hooked_tty_getlin() sets _pending_message only on its restricted arm (js/getline.js:400), so the unrestricted arm that invent.c getobj() uses leaves row 0 blank and the next flush paints nothing there. js/getline.js:395-399 already records the divergence and assigns it to the slice that next owns getobj(); this entry adds the first case that measures it.

Reachable since do_wear.c armoroff()'s delayed branch was ported: a prompted take-off of a suit spends several helpless turns, and hack.c runmode_delay_output() flushes an animation frame in the middle of them, while C still shows the prompt.

Case, expected to fail until the prompt is retained: node scripts/diff-fresh.mjs --seed 7710133 --datetime 20310203040506 --role Knight --gender male --align lawful --name TakeOff --options "pettype:none,!acoustics,!autopickup,!legacy,!tutorial,!splash_screen" --moves ".Tc." -- it reports "First animation mismatch at boundary 4 (segment 1, step 4, key c): Frame 1, cell row 1, column 1 (ch): C: W / JS: (space)", the W of "What do you want to take off? [cdef or ?*]". Everything else matches: PRNG 2609/2609, 5 screens, 5 cursors.

Turn arithmetic decides whether a frame is drawn at all: flags.runmode defaults to RUN_LEAP, so runmode_delay_output() draws only on turns where svm.moves % 7 == 0, and the five turns a ring mail costs from this input sequence span moves 3 to 7. A shorter delay or a different number of leading waits can miss the frame entirely, which is why the take-off matrix keeps its delayed segments on the roles that need no prompt.

deferred.detail:
js/eat.js:1158-1162 prints "Core dumped." for an apple. The reference build prints "Delicious!  Must be a Macintosh!"

eat.c fprefx()'s default arm orders its platform branches so the Mac test wins. At eat.c:2179 the directive `#if defined(MACOS9) || defined(MACOS)` opens a branch whose 2183-2184 arm prints "Delicious!  Must be a Macintosh!" for an APPLE. Only at 2187 does `#ifdef UNIX` open the arm at 2188-2190, which prints "Core dumped." for an APPLE or a PEAR. On a build where both macros are defined the apple never reaches the UNIX arm; the pear does, because the Mac arm does not test for it.

Both macros are defined for the reference build, and it is the pair rather than either alone that makes the ordering bite. include/config.h:18 defines UNIX and nothing undefines it: the only undef is config1.h:64, guarded by MACOS9 or __BEOS__, and neither holds. include/config1.h:43-45 defines MACOS when __APPLE__ and __MACH__, which clang on Darwin supplies with no opt-out; nethack-c/build-recorder.sh forces CC=clang and its Darwin path at 107-117 selects sys/unix/hints/macosx-minimal, so the build goes through sys/unix, keeping UNIX, while config1.h adds MACOS on top. MACOS9 is not defined: config1.h:47-59 sets it only for MPW, THINK_C or MWERKS.

The startup banner is corroboration but not proof, and this entry does not rest on it: "MacOS" comes from global.h:191-193's __APPLE__ test, which is reached before the UNIX fallback at 218-219, so it proves __APPLE__ alone. What settles it is nethack-c/patches/006-nomux-capture.patch, which rewrites a MACOS-guarded TIMED_DELAY test, paired with macosx-minimal:16's -DNO_TIMED_DELAY and its comment at 13-15 explaining that it suppresses the macOS auto-enable of TIMED_DELAY because its presence in the options menu breaks session parity with Linux builds. Nobody writes that patch unless MACOS is live in the build that produced the recordings.

What it costs today is exactly one development screen. seed0016-healer-newmoon-eat-zap emits 14 screens of 36 and matches 13; screen 7 is the only mismatch, C's top line reading "Delicious!  Must be a Macintosh!" against the port's "Core dumped." No random-number call differs, because neither the MACOS arm nor the non-hallucinating UNIX arm draws.

The latent hazard is larger than the visible cost and sits behind the current guard. eat.c:2193's `rnd(100)` is inside the UNIX arm, in its hallucinating half. On this build a hallucinating hero eating an apple takes the MACOS arm at 2183 and draws nothing; only a hallucinating pear draws, and only then does the three-way segmentation-fault wording apply. The comment at js/eat.js:1139-1141 states the opposite, attributing the rnd(100) to the apple, and the UnsupportedEatError at js/eat.js:1145-1147 masks the consequence today because nothing on D:1 causes hallucination. Whoever lifts that guard on the comment's reasoning will implement the Linux random-number stream for an apple and desynchronise the log, which is far more expensive than one wrong line of text.

Closing condition: fprefx()'s default arm selects the MACOS branch for an APPLE and the UNIX branch for a PEAR, matching eat.c:2179-2195 for the build the recorder produces, with a test pinning both strings to values read from the C source; the two wrong comments at js/eat.js:1139-1141 and :1159-1161 are corrected to name the build and to attribute rnd(100) to the pear alone; and the UnsupportedEatError guard is re-scoped to refuse only the hallucinating pear path, which is the only one that draws.

weapon.c mwepgone() (seven lines: take MON_WEP(mon), and if there is one call setmnotwielded(mon, mwep) and set mon->weapon_check = NEED_WEAPON) has no port. js/steal.js:236 supplies it to worn.c extract_from_minvent()'s W_WEP tail as a named refusal, "a monster dropping the weapon it wields", rather than leaving the hook absent: without it a W_WEP object reaching requiredHook() at js/worn.js:392 would throw a bare Error, which js/jsmain.js does not treat as a boundary, so the segment would be discarded rather than ended on its last matching screen.

It is not merely untested, it is unreachable, and that is why it is deferred rather than ported. owornmask gains W_WEP in exactly one place, js/weapon.js:994 inside mon_wield_item(), and that function's only two callers both stop first: js/unported_monster_actions.js:892 refuses "monster wield action" whenever select_hwep() picks a weapon the monster is not already wielding, and :794 refuses "pet weapon selection" on the dogmove.c dog_invent() route. Creation does not wield either -- makemon.c mongets() only calls mpickobj(), and a grep of makemon.c for weapon_check, mon_wield_item and MON_WEP returns nothing. So no C recording can reach the drop: a session that kills a weapon-wielding monster stops at the wield refusal, several turns earlier.

The goal detail of monster-drops-equipped-gear instructed the worker to close this with a fresh differential killing an orc or gnome lord carrying an orcish dagger. That instruction is unfollowable for the reason above; the slice-selector falsified it and the orchestrator and the slice-worker each confirmed it independently before the slice was cut.

No blockedOn is set deliberately. The natural candidate, mon_wield_item, is already defined in js/weapon.js as a partial port, so a blocker naming it would read as landed the day it was written -- the failure the block-deferral help warns about, which has bitten this repository three times. The entry therefore counts toward the monsters sweep threshold, which is honest: it is real debt, not work waiting on someone else.

Cost today: zero recorded steps. Nothing in the development set drops a wielded weapon, and nothing can until the wield boundary moves.

Closing condition: a monster that dies wielding a weapon drops it, with mwepgone() ported over the already-ported setmnotwielded() (js/weapon.js:802) and NEED_WEAPON (js/const.js near :2692), proved by a fresh recorded differential -- which becomes possible only once js/unported_monster_actions.js:892 and :794 admit a wield. Note for whoever takes it: setmnotwielded() is async, so mwepgone() must be, which forces extract_from_minvent() from synchronous to asynchronous and ripples through its ten call sites in scripts/worn.test.mjs.

js/sounds.js:167 paints ambient lines with a hard-coded "You hear " prefix instead of going through pline.c You_hear(), so it skips that function's Unaware branch: C paints "You dream that you hear ..." for a hero who is asleep or fainted (pline.c:446-447). js/mon.js:1290 carries the same defect.

The branch was unreachable until the zap-command goal. fall_asleep() sets u.usleep, so unconscious() answers true and Unaware holds for the ~27 turns a self-zap of sleep costs, which is the first state in the port where an ambient line and an insensible hero can coincide. C's own commented-out block at timeout.c:959-960 names the coupling, which is why it is worth recording rather than leaving to be rediscovered.

It costs nothing measurable today, and that was checked rather than assumed: no development session records a "dream that you hear" line -- grep -c over all 33 session files returns 0 -- and seed0016, the one session that sleeps, records no ambient line at all during the sleep. So this is a live divergence with no observed instance, not a latent one and not a scored loss.

Left unfixed at the zap goal's audit deliberately: js/sounds.js is outside that goal's reviewed range, the fix ports two new You_hear() branches and changes what is rendered, and AGENTS.md wants a fresh C recording before that counts as complete.

Closing condition: ambient lines route through a ported You_hear() that selects C's Unaware wording, with js/mon.js:1290's copy converged onto the same owner, proved by a fresh recorded differential in which a sleeping hero is on a level whose acoustics produce an ambient line -- a fountain level with acoustics enabled and a self-zap of sleep is the cheapest shape. Whoever takes it should check first whether the ambient draw itself is gated on the hero being awake, because if it is, the wording branch may be unreachable from ordinary play and belongs as a named refusal instead.

dogmove.c dog_move():1302 opens its object selection with !Hallucination, so a hallucinating hero reads "Your little dog steps reluctantly onto something." rather than the pile's name. Closing condition: peffect_hallucination() is ported far enough for a hero to quaff a potion of hallucination, and a segment in scripts/run-pet-cursed-step.mjs records a pet stepping onto a cursed pile during that hallucination, matching C call for call.

dogmove.c dog_move():1302-1304 consults glyph_is_object(levl[nix][niy].glyph) before naming the pile a pet stepped onto, and falls back to decl.h:36 something when the hero remembers no object there. js/display.js glyph_is_object() answers that question from a mark object_glyph_info() writes onto every object presentation and remembered_glyph_from_presentation() copies into map memory. Its TRUE arm is proved end to end -- all four segments of scripts/run-pet-cursed-step.mjs name the pile, and a predicate stuck at FALSE would print something instead -- but its FALSE arm has no fresh C case.

The reason is the shape of the C condition rather than a missing port. The FALSE arm needs a square whose map memory holds no object at the moment display.h canseemon() answers TRUE for the pet standing on it, and canseemon() needs cansee() or see_with_infrared() at that same square. In a lit room the hero has already mapped the pile, so the two can only meet where the light does not reach: an unlit room entered with infravision, or a corridor holding a cursed object. mkmap.c litstate_rnd() leaves a D:1 room unlit with probability 1/77 -- rnd(1 + depth) < 11 is always true at depth 1, so rn2(77) is the whole test -- and mklev.c places its random objects inside rooms, at 1159 and 1167, not in corridors. Against a measured base rate of roughly one seed in nine hundred printing this line at all inside forty turns, a scan cannot find the intersection.

Cost today: zero recorded steps. Every development session that reaches this line reaches it in a lit room.

What stands in for it: scripts/dogmove.test.mjs drives the FALSE arm three ways -- an absent remembered glyph, a level whose flags.hero_memory is off, and a hallucinating hero -- and scripts/display-symbols.test.mjs pins the mark itself through object_glyph_info() and remembered_glyph_from_presentation().

Closing condition: a fresh recorded differential in which a pet visible by infravision steps onto a cursed pile the hero has never seen, added to scripts/run-pet-cursed-step.mjs; or, if a deeper reading shows the intersection cannot occur in ordinary play at all, a recorded reason replacing this entry.

The setup needs a remembered pile whose top has changed to a lookalike while the hero could not see the square, then an apply of a lock pick at it. A sighted hero beside a lit room square keeps her memory current through newsym() every turn, so the change has to happen out of sight: a pet picking the top item off an adjacent pile, or a kill that leaves a corpse, while the hero is blind or the square is dark. Nothing in the port reaches that yet -- pet pickup is dog_invent()'s carry arm, whose recorded matrix does not place the pet next to the hero on the turn she applies -- and a natural-seed scan for it would multiply the roughly 1/1000 rate at which a seed reaches the cursed-step line by the chance that the pile top is a lookalike of what was remembered.

Cost today: zero recorded steps. No development session applies a lock pick at a square whose remembered pile top has changed.

Closing condition: a segment in scripts/run-apply-lock-pick.mjs records a hero applying a lock pick at a square whose remembered top object differs from the one now there and draws the same cell, matching C call for call, and the constructed case in scripts/apply-lock-pick.test.mjs keeps its paired negative.

Reaching either needs (svm.moves - age) / (10 + rn2(20)) above 3. scripts/run-eat-corpse.mjs's two waited cases (seeds 7331404 and 7331780) wait 34 turns after the kill and land on 1, which is what makes eat.c:1989's extra draw reachable; about 130 waited turns would exceed 3 for every divisor, and the port stops on an ordinary monster attack roughly 20 turns in. scripts/eat-corpse.test.mjs reaches the tainted stop by setting the carried corpse's age 400 turns back, which puts rotted above 5 whatever the draw is.

cpostfx() (eat.c:1127-1319) ports its default arm and the intrinsic check that follows it. Fourteen species arms stop by name above that: the wraith's pluslvl(), the three human were-forms' set_ulycn(), the nurse's full heal, the stalker's invisibility, the three bats' make_stunned(), the three mimics' nomul() and appearance change, the quantum mechanic's HFast toggle, the lizard's capped timeouts, the four shapechangers' polyself(), the displacer beast, the disenchanter's attrcurse(), the Riders and the two mind flayers. Inside the check, make_hallucinated(), eye_of_newt_buzz(), gainstr() and givit() stop too, so any corpse whose species conveys a resistance, teleport, teleport control or telepathy ends the segment after corpse_intrinsic() has drawn for it -- the killer bee and the acid blob are the two such species a dungeon level one hero meets.

eatcorpse() also stops at rottenfood() (1950), which is 1 in 7 of every fresh rotting corpse, and at the glob, green slime and petrifying arms it refuses before drawing. scripts/eat-corpse.test.mjs pins the rottenfood stop through a corpse marked orotten, which is the branch of that condition C reaches without the rn2(7).

dokick() ports one target: kick_nondoor()'s final else at dokick.c:1251, which reaches kick_dumb(). Twenty-seven refusals above and around it stop by name, each at its own condition and so before that arm draws, prints or writes. dokick()'s nine no-kick guards (:1265-1310) all need the shared display_nhwindow(WIN_MESSAGE, TRUE) at :1314; the steed one needs kick_steed() as well. Its target tests refuse the engulfed rn2(3) at :1334, the levitation bracing block at :1355-1370, the monster arm at :1406 (maybe_kick_monster() and kick_monster()), the off-the-map arm at :1386, the pool and lava arm at :1444, the object pile at :1452 (kick_object()) and the door at :1465 (kick_door()). kick_nondoor() refuses the secret door and secret corridor above their rn2(30), the throne, altar, fountain, grave, iron bars, tree and sink arms, and the wall and upward-stairs arm at :1248; kick_dumb() refuses its own floating recoil at :876-877, which needs hurtle(). kick_ouch() (:880-906) is what most of the rest need, so it is the single largest unblock.

Three cases sit just outside this slice and are recorded here rather than in the passing matrix, because C prints where the port stops. All three use the matrix rc and datetime 20240517131415. Kicking north with the Monk of seed 6600001 ('^D' then 'k') reaches the monster arm, because a monster stands there. Kicking north with the Valkyrie of the same seed reaches the wall arm, whose kick_ouch() opens with the rn2(2) of exercise(A_DEX, FALSE) and prints 'Ouch!  That hurts!' from dokick.c:886. Kicking south-east with the Valkyrie of seed 6600007 ('^D' then 'n') reaches kick_door() on a doorway. scripts/kick-command.test.mjs pins all three as refusals that spend no turn, draw no random number and leave getdir()'s prompt as the last line written.

notes.text: A fourth case joins the three above: kicking north-west with the Valkyrie of seed 6600002 ('^D' then 'y') reaches the object-pile arm, because level generation left an object on that square. It is the one refusal no matrix seed offers, so scripts/kick-command.test.mjs builds its segment through kickSegment() rather than reading it out of the recipe. A fifth, dokick.c:1242-1249's upward staircase, needs no seed of its own: the hero starts on the up staircase, so one step west and a kick east reaches it.

deferred.id: earth_sense() cannot print from its synchronous callers
deferred.detail:
`dungeon.c earth_sense()` (1543-1565) is ported into `js/dungeon.js` with every
gate, but the one line those gates lead to --
`You("sense something below your %s.", makeplural(body_part(FOOT)))` -- raises
`UnsupportedEarthSenseError` instead of printing. That is fail-closed, and it
replaces a fail-open omission, but the line is still unported.

The blocker is shape, not source. `u_on_newpos()` is synchronous, and so are
its two callers: `js/mkmaze.js` calls it at 218 from inside
`put_lregion_here()`, which `place_lregion()` at `js/mkmaze.js:92` reaches, and
`js/stairs.js` calls it at 89 and 101 from `u_on_upstairs()` and
`u_on_dnstairs()`. This port's message owner, `js/tty_message.js ttyPline()`,
is async. Printing here means making level creation async, which is why the
port was declined inside a deferral sweep rather than attempted.

The branch is live rather than dormant, and its gate is the hero's race. Over
the 40 D:1 levels the port generates for seeds 7200000-7200039 it buried 215
objects, 27 of them under a ROOM square, through js/themeroom_fill.js's
`Buried zombies` and `Buried treasure` fills; `js/hack.js domove()` has called
`u_on_newpos()` since 36562b9, so a dwarf hero reaches the notice by walking
onto one. No development session runs a dwarf -- the 33 use elf, gnome and
human -- so nothing recorded reaches it.

No fresh case is recorded, because none was found. A search over seeds
7400000-7400149 for a dwarf Archeologist looked for a buried ROOM or CORR
square reachable from the starting square by one or two straight walks through
squares holding no monster, object or trap, and found none in 150 levels: the
fills put their burials inside a themed room the hero does not start beside.
Closing this needs either a longer path found by a real search, or a recorded
C case built some other way, and then the async conversion above.

This entry restates earth_sense()'s notice is refused rather than printed, whose detail named the wrong file for
place_lregion() and could not be corrected in place. Nothing else changed: the evidence, the
measurements and the closing condition are its own.

Reaching it needs two things at once, and ordinary play at level 1 supplies neither. The corpse needs a petrifying monster killed or wished for, and js/objnam_readobjnam.js:1498 refuses readobjnam()s monster-naming arm, which is the same blocker eat-corpse-arms-without-a-fresh-case carries. Stone resistance has three sources in C and none of them is reachable here: polyself.c:71 PROPSET from resist_from_form(MR_STONE), eat.c givit() from a corpse that conveys MR_STONE -- every one of which petrifies the eater who does not already have it -- and wizcmds.c wiz_intrinsic(), the #wizintrinsic command. js/ ports none of the three; extcmdlist_data.js:165 carries wiz_intrinsic only as a table row.

Close this with a debug-mode recording that grants the intrinsic and wishes for the corpse, once both commands are ported. What it would prove is that the throw spends the turn, prints nothing, and leaves the corpse on the landing square.

display.c newsym() (1013-1024), inside its `if (cansee(x, y))` arm, marks the trap under a displayed monster seen: `if (mon->mtrapped) { struct trap *trap = t_at(x, y); int tt = trap ? trap->ttyp : NO_TRAP; if (tt == BEAR_TRAP || is_pit(tt) || tt == WEB) trap->tseen = 1; }`, then runs _map_location() so the remembered glyph is the trap. pager.c:466-473 repeats the write, and its comment names the mechanism: 'newsym lets you know of the trap'. js/display.js has no mtrapped term anywhere -- grep -c mtrapped js/display.js returns 0 -- and both newsym() sites, js/display.js:2089-2103 and the state-parameterised sibling at :1673-1678, compute `t_at(x, y)` and then test `trap?.tseen` with no mtrapped clause.

The gap costs a wrong screen and wrong map memory. js/trap_effects.js:508-524 sets mtmp.mtrapped and calls seetrap() only when in_sight, so a catch the hero did not watch leaves trap.tseen false. The hero then walks into view: C sets tseen and files the trap glyph into memory, the port files the floor glyph. If the monster leaves the square before its next m_move() -- the hero kills it -- C redraws the trap and the port redraws floor, and the memory stays wrong for the rest of the level. The port only sets tseen at the monster's next m_move(), through js/monmove.js:2506's mintrap() and js/trap_effects.js:923-926's seetrap().

Found by the correctness pass over eb3a084..bd50af3 and confirmed against the C source. It is old, not introduced by that range, but the range is what made it reachable in ordinary play: before it, a monster could not stay trapped across turns. Every Knight segment in scripts/run-monster-bear-trap.mjs catches the pony in sight, where trapeffect_bear_trap()'s own seetrap() has already set tseen, which is why the validation could not see it.

Deferred rather than fixed in the goal's audit-fix commit because .agents/review.md returns a finding to Implementation when it 'requires a new upstream function family or branch': newsym()'s mtrapped arm is a branch no goal has ported, and display.c is not among bear-trap-capture's owners. The pass therefore does not claim to cover it.

Closing condition: js/display.js newsym() carries display.c:1017-1023's write at both sites, for BEAR_TRAP, is_pit() and WEB, before it computes the remembered glyph; a unit case with a visible mtrapped monster on an unseen bear trap asserts trap.tseen and the remembered trap glyph; and a fresh recorded C case catches a monster out of sight, brings the hero into view and kills it in one blow, matching C's trap glyph on the vacated square. The write draws nothing and spends no random-number call, so it costs no frame.

trap.c mintrap():3771-3772 writes "%s pulls free of the %s." through trapname(BEAR_TRAP, FALSE), and nothing in the repository asserts it. Measured at be31599: the only segment in scripts/run-monster-bear-trap.mjs whose roll frees its victim is seed 7005082, and no captured screen on either side contains "pulls free" -- C's line needs canseemon() and that pony is out of sight by the turn the roll lands. The five other matrix segments never escape. seed0004-feeding-pony's own escape at step 83 is silent for the same reason. So trapname()'s only consumer in the port has no end-to-end coverage at all, and the matrix test now asserts the silence rather than the line. Closing condition: a fresh recorded C case keeps a trapped monster in the hero's sight across the 1-in-40 roll -- roughly 60 waiting turns gives about 80 per cent -- and matches C's escape line call for call and screen for screen; bound and record the search domain first, as .agents/validation.md requires.

js/allmain.js:686-688 chooses the elapsed turn's message and status seams with `message: planning ? silentMessage : ttyPline` and `statusRefresh: planning ? () => {} : () => bot()`. js/teleport.js mnexto() ends by assigning `relocated.mux = state.u.ux; relocated.muy = state.u.uy` as a stand-in for the set_apparxy() call C makes inside rloc_to(). js/monmove.js already exports a ported set_apparxy(), tested by nine cases in scripts/monmove.test.mjs, so the stand-in duplicates code the port has. Commit 2c866f5 re-derived the caller inventory into a comment and stated the precondition, but a comment is all that holds it: a caller whose monster is blind, or one reached while the hero is invisible, displaced or underwater, would take set_apparxy()'s displacement path and spend an rn2 the stand-in does not. Replacing the two assignments with a set_apparxy() call would remove the precondition entirely. It changes production behavior only if some caller does not in fact take an early return, so it needs its own differential across all three callers (js/allmain.js:217, js/dog.js:796, js/do.js:1406) rather than a test-only change; that is why this lane did not do it. Found by the tests deferral burn-down.

js/eat.js done_eating():1889, `state.context.victual = zero_victual();`, is a mutation survivor. Deleting it leaves all 24 tests in scripts/eat-occupation.test.mjs green, including the two that assert `assert.deepEqual(game.context.victual, zero_victual())` after a meal, and the victual is still fully zeroed at the end of the new two-meal segment. The reason is that done_eating()'s useup(piece) reaches js/invent.js obfree():1677-1680, which calls food_disappears() (js/eat.js:901-903), and that zeroes the same struct one call earlier. C has the same double write -- shk.c obfree():1195-1196 calls eat.c food_disappears(), which assigns zero_victual, and eat.c done_eating():572 assigns it again -- so this is faithful redundancy rather than a defect, and no ported path reaches done_eating() without obfree() running first. The likely right resolution is to record it as a permanent survivor with that reason rather than to chase a test for it; filing it so the next mutation run over js/eat.js does not rediscover it cold. Found by the tests deferral burn-down.

js/exper.js experience()'s repeat-kill loop condition `tmp > 1` yields a permanent mutation survivor that no assertion can kill. `tmp >= 1` returns the same value for every input: tmp is at least 1 on entry, Math.trunc((1 + 1) / 2) is 1, and i and nk are dead after the loop, so the extra iterations change nothing observable. Exhaustive simulation over tmp 1..3000 and nk 0..400, covering the one-byte kill count the caller passes, found no differing pair. Every future mutation run over that line will report it, and each report costs a trace: the deferral mutate-sites-reports-a-false-survivor was opened on exactly that trace. Record the reason where a review will find it, or exclude the site. Found by the tests deferral burn-down.

scripts/mutate-sites.mjs mutates relational operators, `&&`, `||`, boolean literals and integer bounds, so it cannot express dropping a whole disjunct or a statement, which is the defect shape two correctness passes over the melee subsystem kept finding. This is the surviving half of mutate-sites-reports-a-false-survivor, whose other claim did not reproduce, and it is the reason that entry gave for mutation score and test quality being close to uncorrelated in that range: eed732b3..5168910 scored 253 of 220 killed with six real test defects in it, and 5168910..dc31f03 scored 68 of 144 surviving with no production defect. A deletion kind, dropping one operand of `&&` or `||`, would let the number speak to the defects the passes actually find. Costs a new site kind, its enumeration, and its report labels. Found by the tests deferral burn-down.

js/mthrowu.js blocking_terrain():40-41 reads an absent GameMap cell as C's leading !isok(x, y) at mthrowu.c:1284, and the two are not the same set. cmd.c isok():4329 is x >= 1 && x <= COLNO - 1 && y >= 0 && y <= ROWNO - 1, so C rejects column zero; js/game.js GameMap.at():78-81 rejects only x < 0 and x >= COLNO, so column zero has a cell and the port falls through to IS_OBSTRUCTED(levl[0][y].typ). A count of 2 or more before any extcmdlist[] row other than the two carrying occupation text refuses at js/cmd.js rhack(), where cmd.c parse():5142-5144 has left gm.multi above 0. Two recorded cases sit just outside the goal and cannot match the C reference yet. Both were recorded at seed 9310001, datetime 20260814101500, a Valkyrie with pettype:none and !acoustics, moves prefixed by the space that dismisses startup output; the count digits are typed at a prompt whose row 0 already reads 'Be careful!  New moon tonight.'.

1. ' 12i'. C paints 'Count: 12' at the second digit and then opens the inventory once: doinv() answers ECMD_OK, so rhack():3814 reaches reset_cmd_vars() and zeroes gm.multi before moveloop_core() can repeat anything. The port stops at the 'i' with 4 of C's 5 screens, its message row still holding 'Count: 12'.

The stop became reachable when cmd.c rhack():3728-3729's set_occupation() call landed: a counted command is the first thing this port leaves with gm.multi above 0 and neither svc.context.run nor svc.context.travel set, which is exactly the state the guard admits. allmain.c regen_hp():678 and regen_pw():617 are the two callers, both inside the same elapsed turn that then runs moveloop_core()'s occupation arm.

deferred.detail:
js/cfgfiles.js config_error_add() keeps the whole message. C truncates twice
before it reaches a screen:

- pline.c vconfig_error_add() formats into a BIGBUFSZ buffer and then writes
  `buf[BUFSZ - 1] = '\\0'`, cutting the message at 255 bytes.
- pline.c vpline() (212-225) cuts anything still longer than BUFSZ - 1 and
  rewrites the tail as `...` plus the final three characters, so a long
  offending line echoed by `pline("\\n%s", origline)` arrives elided rather
  than merely clipped. origline holds up to 4 * BUFSZ bytes, so a
  1023-character configuration line reaches this.

Nothing shorter than 256 bytes can tell the difference, and the recorded
screens truncate at 80 columns anyway, so this shows up only in a message the
port would raw-print onto a second and third row where C prints one. No
development session has such a line; a fresh case would need an rc statement
of its own.

notes.text: Read at 9a25f0b: this is not observable on a recorded screen. Patch 006's nomux_raw_putch drops any byte past column 79 and never wraps (nethack-c/patches/006-nomux-capture.patch:351-358), so both vconfig_error_add()'s 255-byte cut and vpline()'s three-dot elision land off-screen in C and in the port alike. Its only observable route is a pline() after the window system is up, which is the interactive O command. So it cannot close on a fresh differential and wants a note or a blockedOn rather than a slice. Also correcting the record's citation: vconfig_error_add() is at cfgfiles.c:1875, not pline.c; the moved-to-pline.c comment at cfgfiles.c:1542 is stale. vpline() is genuinely pline.c.

deferred.detail:
js/options.js stripNegation() steps over whitespace after each negation prefix;
options.c:539-542 does not.

    while ((*opts == '!') || !strncmpi(opts, "no", 2)) {
        opts += (*opts == '!') ? 1 : (opts[2] != '-') ? 2 : 3;
        negated = !negated;
    }

C advances by exactly one, two or three bytes, so `OPTIONS=! time` leaves
opts as " time". optlen is then length_without_val(" time", 5) = 5, and
strncmpi(name, " time", 5) matches no allopt[] row, so the statement is
"Unknown option ' time'." and flags.time keeps its default. The port trims the
space, matches `time` and sets it.

The port's other parseoptions() port, the one doset() reaches
(js/options.js:3905-3911), already strips the prefixes exactly as C does, so
the two disagree with each other as well as with C. Fixing the rc-side one is
a few lines, but it changes which statements match, so it wants its own
development-score check rather than a ride on an unrelated slice. No recorded
session spells a negation this way: a census of the 33 development sessions
finds 67 negated OPTIONS elements over four option names -- autopickup,
legacy, splash_screen and tutorial -- and none carries whitespace after the
prefix.

An OPTIONS statement that reaches one of allopt[]'s two pfx rows without
naming a condition this port recognizes still stops the segment, at
js/options.js applyOption()'s `unported prefix option` refusal.

options.c reaches those rows two ways (556-580): str_start_is() accepts any
suffix of the prefix, and match_optname() accepts a leading substring of the
prefix name itself down to minmatch. So `cond`, `cond_`, `cond_bogus`,
`cond_blind:on`, `font` and `fontbogus:value` all match, and each one then
gets its row's handler. pfxfn_cond_() (options.c:2545-2588) hands the whole
statement to botl.c parse_cond_option(), which answers 1 for a suffix no
condtests[] row matches and 2 for a statement no longer than "cond_", and the
handler reports "Unknown condition option %s (%d)". Because pfx_match is set,
options.c:675-682 then adds a second error, "bad option suffix variation
'%s'", over the statement text truncated at its first colon. pfxfn_font() is
not ported at all.

Two errors from one statement is a shape no other rc path in this port
produces, and the second one needs pfx_match carried out of the match loop.
Until then the refusal is named rather than reported as an unknown option,
which would be the wrong message for every one of these.

Inputs and expected C output, taken from the source above rather than a
recording: `OPTIONS=cond_bogus` gives
" * Line 1: Unknown condition option cond_bogus (1)." followed by
" * Line 1: bad option suffix variation 'cond_bogus'.", and `OPTIONS=cond`
gives only " * Line 1: Unknown condition option cond (2)." because it matched
through match_optname() with pfx_match still false.

Reporting from the table as it stands would wrongly flag HACKDIR, BOULDER, HILITE_STATUS, WARNINGS, WIZKIT and the rest: js/options.js CONFIG_STATEMENTS holds 13 rows against the 31 rows of cfgfiles.c config_line_stmt[] a player's rc file can match (the whole table less its 28 syscnf_only ones). notes.text: Two of botl.c parse_status_hl1()'s bounds are unreachable while HILITE_STATUS goes undispatched, and become reachable the day it lands, so the slice that adds the row owes them a case. parseoptions() (options.c:521-525) refuses an element over BUFSZ/2, reporting 'Option too long, max length is 128 characters' before any handler runs, and 'hilite_status:' spends 14 of those 128 bytes. A hilite_status value therefore cannot exceed 114 bytes through OPTIONS, which puts both bounds out of reach: parse_status_hl1()'s per-field 'ccount < QBUFSZ - 2' needs 126 characters in one field, and its 'fldnum < MAX_THRESH' needs 21 '/' separators, at which point parse_status_hl2() reads hsbuf[21], one past the array. Measured at seed 3310277 and 19960229180000: a 163-byte OPTIONS element reported the length error, and a 149-byte one reporting the same error was reduced to 86 bytes to reach the field limit, where C answered "Unknown behavior '<six uninitialized bytes>'". cfgfiles.c has no such cap on a statement's own value, so HILITE_STATUS=... reaches parse_status_hl1() with the whole line. This note records the finding for that slice; status-hilite-rules-still-fail-closed left both bounds ported and untested for the same reason.

deferred.detail: js/options.js bind_key() computes the parenthesized parameter for its three diagnostics and then drops it, where cmd.c bind_key() (2706-2708) stores a 30-byte copy of it into the matched key's struct Cmd_bind param field (include/func_tab.h:37). Its one reader is cmd.c dotoggleoption() (1376-1384), which hands gc.cmd_bind->param to toggle_bool_option(); with no param stored it prints "Use #optionsfull to set any option instead." instead. Nothing in this port dispatches the #toggle extended command yet, so the store has no consumer and lands with dotoggleoption().

js/options.js statusConditionNames() and parseStatusHiliteRule() throw optionError() for an unknown status condition, alias or threshold, where cfgfiles.c reports a configuration error and reads on. This is the defect class a634c32 fixed for BIND and OPTIONS statements, one subsystem over: a mistyped STATUSHILITE rule costs the whole segment above runSegment()'s catch instead of one line of the error block. Closing it needs no unported C. Found by the fix agent's sweep for unguarded rc-text indexes during the correctness pass over 1842f5e3..a634c32, and not covered by any entry open at that time.

js/options.js ports cmd.c bind_mousebtn() (2623-2659) for its answer alone, so parsebindings() reports and falls through exactly as C does, but the gc.Cmd.mousebtn[] store the C function writes has no JavaScript home. An accepted mouse binding therefore leaves no state behind. Nothing reads that array until mouse input is ported, so the gap changes no observable behavior today; this entry exists so it has a durable record when it does.

js/options.js MENU_HEADING_ATTRIBUTES maps 'dim', 'italic' and 'blink' to ATR_NONE, because recorder patch 006 retains only bold, underline and inverse. That is right for menu_headings, where optfn_menu_headings() stores one attribute, and wrong for a status highlight: botl.c parse_status_hl2():3028-3040 sets HL_DIM, HL_ITALIC or HL_BLINK alongside whatever came before, while ATR_NONE alone reaches 'disp_attrib = HL_NONE', which discards the attributes named earlier in the same action. The port therefore reads 'dim' as that discard.

Measured at seed 3310277 and 19960229180000. OPTIONS=hilite_status:hitpoints/always/bold&dim draws HP with ESC[1m in C and with no attribute in the port, because 'dim' cleared the bold that 'bold' had set. The colour survives either way, so OPTIONS=hilite_status:hitpoints/always/red&italic matches.

Fixing it means separating the two readings: parse_status_hl2() and parse_condition() need an answer that distinguishes a tty-invisible attribute from ATR_NONE, which menuHeadingAttribute() cannot give while it is shared with parseMenuHeadingStyle(). It sits outside status-hilite-rules-still-fail-closed, which ports the error arms.

The port answers Return with "Unknown command '^M'." where C runs a command. js/tty_rawprint.js nomux_raw_putch() stores one screen cell per byte, which is
what recorder patch 006 does, but the recorded screen a byte grid produces is
not a byte grid. The capture writes the shadow buffer's bytes to a file, and
the session loader reads that file as UTF-8, so a two-byte sequence in adjacent
cells arrives as one character and the recorded row is shorter than 80. The
port's cells hold one JavaScript character per byte, and frozen/terminal.js
serializes each cell on its own, so the same sequence arrives as two.

Measured, not inferred. A fresh case at seed 5128094, 20120919081000, over an
rc whose second line is `OPTIONS=zqxjé` matches C on every random-number call
and every cursor and diverges at the first byte of the é: `Cell row 2, column
13 (ch): C "é", JS "Ã"`. The statement echo config_erradd() prints is enough to
reach it, so any non-ASCII byte in an erroring rc line costs the rest of that
row and every row below it.

Nothing in the port decides this on its own: matching C means the cells a
multi-byte sequence occupies have to serialize as one character, and
frozen/terminal.js is judge-owned. The fix is therefore in what the port puts
in the cells, not in how they are written out, and it wants a decision about
what the raw cursor column then counts. No development session has a non-ASCII
rc line.

notes.text: Read at 9a25f0b: the port owes this fix, but it is not a port of any C, which is why it does not fit this goal's closing condition. The measuring chain is closed at both ends: patch 006 stores one char per cell and emits it byte by byte, and frozen/session_loader.mjs:107 reads the session file as UTF-8. AGENTS.md makes the patched C's output the behavior to match and frozen/ is judge-supplied, so neither end can change, and changing the recorder would invalidate every recording including the holdout. js/tty_rawprint.js nomux_raw_putch() is already a faithful line-for-line port that stores a byte per cell because C does. What is missing is a compensation for a lossy capture: place a whole decoded character in one cell and shift the row's tail, while the recorded cursor still counts bytes. There is no C function to name as its closing condition, so if it survives this goal it should be re-scoped as a display-fidelity entry rather than an unported-behavior one.

and alignment names from the compiled-in tables, all ASCII. svp.plname is the

Derived from the C, not measured: a fresh case cannot isolate it while
raw-print-splits-a-multibyte-character stands, because the same non-ASCII name

together.

notes.text:
Closed. The record names role.c plsel_startup_msg(); no such function exists.
'grep -rln plsel_startup_msg nethack-c/upstream/' exits 1 with no output. The
line numbers 2821 and 2828 are right and the owner is plsel_startmenu(), at
role.c:2806.

The record also called the defect unwitnessable while
raw-print-splits-a-multibyte-character stands. That is wrong, and the reason it
is wrong is worth keeping: the header is a menu line, and process_menu_window()
hands nomux_putch() one signed char per byte, so every high-bit byte is below 32
there and leaves its shadow cell blank. The recorded observable is therefore
entirely ASCII, unlike tty_raw_print()'s, which patch 006 casts to unsigned
char and stores. A fresh case at seed 4820577, 20340517080910, over an rc whose
only setting is OPTIONS=name:Aardvarkbcdefghijkem with an e-acute, matched every
call, screen and cursor after the fix and diverged at one cell before it.

Closing it cost two more corrections in js/tty_menu.js, both the same C fact:
tty_end_menu() measures and cuts a stored line with strlen(), and
process_menu_window() advances one column per byte. Without them the fix moved
the whole menu window one column instead of matching C.

deferred.detail:
js/tty_menu.js searchItemText() and sourceMenuLineText() both rebuild the line
tty_end_menu() stored and cut it with String.prototype.slice at columns - 2,
which counts UTF-16 code units. wintty.c:2728-2733 writes the NUL at
curr->str[ttyDisplay->cols - 2], a byte offset, and process_menu_window()'s
MENU_SEARCH arm matches its pattern against that cut string.

ttyMenuLayout() was corrected to bytes in the same commit that fixed
role.c plsel_startmenu()'s "%.20s", so the stored-line cut is now spelled in
two units inside one file. Only the search and PICK_ONE paths still read the
code-unit form, and they diverge from C only for a stored line over 78 bytes
that also holds a multibyte character -- an object label or fruit name longer

Closes when one helper owns the cut and all three call sites take it.

wintty.c process_text_window() (1808-1833) sends only the first byte of each
line through g_putch() when its high bit is set, and recorder patch 006 strips
that bit before nomux_putch() stores it: a line beginning 0xC3 0xA9 records 'C'
in the first cell and leaves the second as the clear left it.

js/tty_menu.js has two ports of that loop. writeRecorderTtyWindowLine(), which
displayTtyMenuTextWindow() uses for look_here()'s window, models the first-byte
arm. displayTtyTextWindow(), the paged NHW_TEXT variant, draws through
writeStyledText() instead, which has no first-byte arm and now skips a leading
high-bit byte rather than writing 'C' there.

That skip arrived with the commit that made writeStyledText() count bytes,
which the character-selection header needed; before it the same cell held the
whole character and every later cell was one column left, so the arm is newly
wrong in one cell and newly right in the rest. Nothing reaches it: every
NHW_TEXT line the port draws starts with ASCII.

Closes when the two ports of process_text_window()'s loop become one that
carries both the line's attribute and the first-byte arm.

notes.text:
Correction to the first paragraph of `detail`: it names the wrong cell, and
neither port models the arm.

Recorder patch 006 hooks nomux_putch() three times on the path
process_text_window()'s draw loop takes. Both putchar siblings inside the loop
wrap the call as `{ int svx = ttyDisplay->curx; ttyDisplay->curx--;
nomux_putch(*cp); ttyDisplay->curx = svx; }`. The third hook sits inside
g_putch() itself and has no such compensation. The loop increments curx in its
own condition -- `*cp && (int) ++ttyDisplay->curx < (int) ttyDisplay->cols` --
so throughout byte k's body curx stands one column past the column putchar()
prints that byte in. The compensated hooks therefore record byte k in its own
column and the g_putch() hook records one column to the right.

So a line beginning 0xC3 0xA9 leaves the first cell as the clear left it and
records 'C' in the second. The 0xA9 that follows cannot overwrite that 'C':
nomux_putch() takes an int, `*cp` is a signed char, and the guard
`if (!ttyDisplay || ch < 32) return` drops every negative one.

writeRecorderTtyWindowLine() writes the stripped byte at `column + index`,
which is the first cell, and writeStyledText() writes it nowhere. Both are
wrong by one cell in opposite directions, so this entry blesses neither port;
the merged loop it asks for has to place that byte one column to the right of
the byte's own column.

A second divergence between the same two ports, and a second requirement on
the merged loop.

nomux_putch()'s `ch < 32` guard drops a control byte for the same reason it
drops a high-bit one, and neither reaches the shadow grid.
writeRecorderTtyWindowLine() writes every byte below 0x80 through
display.setCell(), control bytes included, so it fills a cell C leaves as the
preceding clear left it. writeStyledText() drops them, through the
`bytes[index] < 0x20` half of its skip; scripts/tty-menu.test.mjs
'process_menu_window emits no cell for a control byte' pins that half.

The merged loop therefore has to drop every byte below 0x20 as well as every
high-bit byte that is not the g_putch() first byte, on top of placing that
first byte in the column named in the note above.

notes.text: Correction on both scope and severity, from the slice-selector's reading at ea8188f2, which I verified. Scope: the entry names one site and there are five, all adding a negated blocked term to a two-disjunct macro. js/dogmove.js:219; js/mhitm.js:100, whose reader is mhitm.c:436; js/mhitu.js:96 via activeHeroProperty() at :618, whose reader is mhitu.c:803; and js/monmove.js:408 and :424, both propertyActive(state, CONFLICT, true), against monmove.c:1302 and :1318. Four other sites already spell it correctly, at js/mon.js:392, js/monmove.js:1697 and :2597, and js/unported_monster_actions.js:175, which is what makes this one C rule answered two ways rather than a consistent house style. Severity, downgraded: C never blocks CONFLICT, so the extra conjunct cannot change an answer today. youprop.h defines a blocked alias for exactly six properties, at :90 BLINDED, :181 CLAIRVOYANT, :197 INVIS, :209 STEALTH, :239 LEVITATION and :252 FLYING; `grep -rn BConflict nethack-c/upstream/` returns nothing and exits 1; and the only writers are worn.c:38-44 w_blocks(), which yields INVIS, CLAIRVOYANT or BLINDED, and polyself, which sets FLYING, LEVITATION and STEALTH. I read w_blocks() myself and confirm those three are all it can produce. So this is a spelling defect that no input reaches, not the live divergence the original detail implies, and its closing condition should pin all five sites at once.

Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: blocksMove() reads loc.doormask while level generation writes loc.flags, so its closed-door arm is dead on every generated door.
rejections.counterEvidence: The reading is correct but neither blocksMove() nor doorMask() is changed by this range, and the dead arm is protective: requireSimpleHeroDestination() refuses closed, locked, and trapped masks through doorMask() itself. Both proposed repairs create new defects. Renaming the generated field is wrong for the C union, where include/rm.h overloads the same flags bitfield as doormask, altarmask, wall_info, ladder, drawbridgemask, and looted. Routing a closed door into domove()'s blocked branch produces a silent zero-time stop where C prints 'That door is closed.', because the ported test_move() returns true for a non-STONE, non-wall square. Reopen only with a ported closed-door owner to attach it to.

passes.head: eb7e17ec72379124ff7bab6f80ff4b3f773393ef
passes.evidence: Two audit-diff-correctness passes covering this range end to end: a full pass over 03c2add..e05118c (four finders; 26 raw, 21 deduplicated, 19 confirmed, all applied at a6bd5af) and a light pass over 4fc57d8..03c2add (three finders; 7 raw, 6 deduplicated, 4 confirmed, three applied at eb7e17e and one deferred as a verified pre-existing gap). Validation at eb7e17e: 1,724 tests, four generated-data checks, check:namespace-members, and four fresh matrices re-recorded against C (no-time commands 29,459 PRNG calls with 71 screens; repeated simple commands 104,649 with 2,541; second complete turn 46,255 with 54; first-command closure 311,439 with 119). productionDefects.summary: look_here() threw on any corpse, but C's feel_cockatrice(otmp, FALSE) is a no-op unless will_feel_cockatrice() holds, so walking onto an ordinary corpse aborted the segment, and after its messages had already printed.
rhack()'s look dispatch called dolook() outside failClosedCommand(), so every unported look_here() branch escaped runSegment() instead of stopping retryably.
Return and Linefeed did not finish a PICK_ONE menu without an empty completion, though process_menu_window() finishes on \0, \n, \r and Space alike.
The packorder option was parsed and discarded, so display_pickinv() would have listed the default class order for a session that set it; change_inv_order() is unported.
The generated CMAP_EXPLANATIONS entry for S_web held "',  S_web, " because the extractor scanned the whole entry for its last quoted string and that entry's character literal is a double quote.
objnam.c just_an() was ported twice in js/objnam.js.
vtense()'s es and s branches appended lowercase literals where C writes them through Strcasecpy(), dropping case propagation.
dfeature_at() read the door mask as doormask||flags, reversing the precedence every other reader in the port uses.
js/hack.js passed a literal 0 for look_here()'s obj_cnt where pickup.c check_here() passes the counted objects, which pile_limit is compared against.
display_pickinv() formatted names one at a time, and formatting marks a type discovered, so a pack whose later item could not be named left the earlier ones discovered and still refused the command.

Verified pre-existing: the identical probe at the parent produces identical output. The fix must be a preflight, because a live conversion is not atomic.

passes.head: 60bf2c3cf1fc8d7313970a91417547af466206c3
passes.evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the no-time-command goal: dodiscovered(), dospellmenu(), doattributes() and enlightenment(), plus weapon_descr()'s move into js/weapon.js. Four finders ran (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency were not enabled, because the range adds no hot-path work and no new shared mutable state. 17 raw findings, 16 after deduplication, 14 confirmed and all 14 applied across 7d11c53 and 2adc5af; 2 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. The four production defects were Fixed_abil read as intrinsic-or-extrinsic, a stop on every wielded towel rather than a wet one, a deafness guard that missed u.uroleplay.deaf, and can_advance() refusing on speedy ahead of the three tests C answers FALSE from. Validation at 2adc5af: 1,765 tests passing, four generated-data checks, check:namespace-members, development score unchanged at 98,759 PRNG values and 286 screens and cursors with no session regressed, and the no-time matrix matching 71,967 calls with 158 screens and cursors across 29 segments.

productionDefects.summary: one_characteristic() tested Fixed_abil through hasProperty(), which ORs the intrinsic and the extrinsic. youprop.h:385 defines the macro as the extrinsic alone, with no HFixed_abil term, so an intrinsic in that slot stopped the command where C prints the six characteristics.

weapon_insight() refused every wielded towel, but obj.h defines is_wet_towel(o) as otyp == TOWEL && spe > 0 and weapon.c lists TOWEL among weapon_descr()'s P_NONE overrides, so a dry towel prints "You are wielding a towel."

The deafness guard read u.uprops[DEAF] only, but youprop.h:245 defines Deaf as (HDeaf || EDeaf || u.uroleplay.deaf). OPTIONS=deaf sets the third term alone, so the port printed a window where C prints " You are deaf."

can_advance() refused on speedy before evaluating the three tests C answers FALSE from, so a restricted or maxed skill ended the segment instead of answering FALSE. C's shortcut is wizard && speedy and sits after those tests.

rejections.summary: status_enlightenment() accepts mode and never reads it, said to hide that C's `boolean magic = (mode & MAGICENLIGHTENMENT)` gate on the Fumbling, Sleepy and Hunger arms was replaced by unconditional stops.
rejections.counterEvidence: insight.c:728 declares basics_enlightenment(int mode UNUSED, int final), so upstream itself carries an unread mode on a section function and mirroring the C signature is the faithful choice; the port also threads mode to one_characteristic(), which reads it. The over-broad stops fail closed for states no supported path can produce, so no screen, message or random-number call differs from the C. The proposed lint check would equally flag a faithful port of insight.c:728. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input that makes an unread mode change output.

rejections.summary: None of js/insight.js's 16 stops is exercised by any test, and the fail-closed property is said not to hold because 12 of the 16 run after basics_enlightenment() has called find_ac().
rejections.counterEvidence: find_ac()'s write is conditional on armorClass !== u.uac, matching do_wear.c:2508-2510 at the same point in the same sequence, and js/u_init_inventory_attrs.js is untouched by the reviewed range. Measured on a live game at a ready D:1 prompt, u.uac and disp.botl read the same before and after an extra find_ac() call, so no stop leaves state the prompt did not already have; C calls find_ac() before the same points regardless. The residual true claim, that no test threw a stop, was addressed separately: the applied fixes add tests that throw the towel, stuck_ring() and deafness stops. Do not reopen without a state where find_ac() writes before a stop and the write is observable.
