Every port site that touches gb.bhitpos or gn.notonhead writes before it reads, so there is no reader that the omission can mislead, and the concrete trace offered (a long-worm pet leaving gn.notonhead true) is refuted by the writer at js/dogmove.js:228 setting it on every use. Counter-evidence: `grep -rn "bhitpos" js/` yields writes at js/dog.js:318-320, js/dogmove.js:224-226 and 895-897, a structural clone at js/unported_monster_actions.js:459, and — in js/mhitm.js:74 and :101 — only comment text, not a read. `grep -rn "notonhead" js/` yields js/dog.js:322-324 (writes then returns the value it just wrote), js/dogmove.js:228 and :899 (writes). No site reads either value before writing it, so the finding's own premise ("unobservable today only Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: js/apply.js:186 (correctness) — `use_stethoscope()` never models C's `interference` initializer, whose `rn2()` is drawn at function entry — before the nohands/Deaf/freehand guards and before `getdir()` — so the swallowed-hero refusal at line 186 sits after three return paths that can leave the port one RNG draw behind C with no fa
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: Same refutation as index 1: the draw the port is said to skip cannot occur, because C short-circuits it behind u.uswallow and nothing in the port writes u.uswallow truthy. The stronger wording here — that the refusal "fails open for four of C's exits" — is wrong for every state the running game can build, since on those states C makes no draw either. Counter-evidence: apply.c:324-325 `(u.uswallow && is_whirly(u.ustuck->data) && !rn2(Role_if(PM_HEALER) ? 10 : 3))`; `&&` short-circuits. `grep -rn "uswallow" js/` shows the only assignments in the entire port are js/u_init.js:161 `uswallow: false` and js/mon.js:260 `state.u.uswallow = 0;`. The finding's own grep reaches the same conclusion ("the path is latent"). The quoted C excerpt is also misattributed to apply.c:318-337; the initializer is at 324-325.  ||  causality refute: Introduced-by-the-range holds, but materiality  Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: js/insight.js:843 (readability) — The comment above `UNPORTED_USTATUS_CONDITIONS` claims "The rows follow C's order inside ustatusline(), because C builds `info` by appending in that order", but three of C's `info` writers are checked after the whole array, so the file's actual stop order is not C's append order.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The comment does not assert what the finding refutes. It says "The rows follow C's order", scoped to the twelve array rows, and those twelve are in C's relative append order (Sick, Stoned, Slimed, Strangled, Vomiting, Confusion, Blind, Stunned, Wounded_legs, Glib, Fast, Invis). It never claims the whole stop sequence, including the three non-property checks below the loop, reproduces C's append order. The WOUNDED_LEGS point is likewise already covered by the comment's own closing sentence. Counter-evidence: js/insight.js:861-863 lists GLIB, FAST, INVIS in the same relative order C appends them at insight.c:3452, 3456, 3462. The comment at js/insight.js:849-850 states "So each stop can only fire early, never late", which is exactly the disposition of the WOUNDED_LEGS row that drops C's `!u.usteed` conjunct at insight.c:3438 — the stop is deliberately wider, and the commen Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: js/insight.js:862 (variable-trace) — UNPORTED_USTATUS_CONDITIONS lists FAST and INVIS before the u.utrap, u.uundetected and disguised checks, but C appends those fragments in the opposite order — contradicting the table's own comment that the rows follow C's order.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: The range introduces the arrangement, but the impact is not material. Every row and every following check throws the same UnsupportedEnlightenmentError and ends the segment, so the order changes only the diagnostic string. The remaining harm — a future porter converting stops into appends in the listed order — is speculative and contradicted by the port's governing rule to implement from the C function. Counter-evidence: js/insight.js:872-891: all five checks below the rows raise UnsupportedEnlightenmentError. The finding states it itself: "No output or PRNG effect today, because every row and every following check raises the same UnsupportedEnlightenmentError and ends the segment." AGENTS.md: "Implement from the C function, never from observed output."  ||  resolution refute: The validation is tautological. Asserting that a hero with u.utrap and FAST raises 'the trappe Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: js/insight.js:881 (correctness) — `ustatusline()` compares the raw `youmonst.m_ap_type` field against `M_AP_NOTHING`, but C's `U_AP_TYPE` is `gy.youmonst.m_ap_type & M_AP_TYPMASK` (`monst.h:71`); the unmasked read answers truthy whenever the `M_AP_F_DKNOWN` bit (0x8) is set on an otherwise-`M_AP_NOTHING` hero.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The unmasked read is only a divergence if M_AP_F_DKNOWN can be set on the hero's youmonst, and it cannot be in either program. Counter-evidence: `grep -rn 'youmonst\.m_ap_type' nethack-c/upstream/src/` returns only whole-value assignments — hack.c:2960, potion.c:214, mhitu.c:676, timeout.c:397, polyself.c:226/782/1794/1867, teleport.c:495, monmove.c:611, eat.c:173/1219 — every one storing M_AP_NOTHING, M_AP_OBJECT or M_AP_MONSTER, never OR-ing a flag. The single C writer of the flag, pager.c:372 inside object_from_map(), operates on the `mtmp` it takes from the map ('there might be a mimic here posing as an object', pager.c:305), and the hero is never in the monster chain, so it can never be &gy.youmonst. On the port side `grep -rn 'm_ap_type' js/` shows js/insight.js:881 is the only mention of youmonst.m_ap_type at all — no writer exists. Masked and unmasked reads there Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: js/insight.js:881 (variable-trace) — ustatusline() reads `youmonst.m_ap_type` raw instead of through the canonical `M_AP_TYPE()` helper, so the M_AP_F_DKNOWN flag bit alone would make it report the hero as disguised.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: Same trace as finding 9: the masked and unmasked reads cannot disagree, and the supporting claim about the const.js helper's provenance is wrong. Counter-evidence: C sets M_AP_F_DKNOWN only at pager.c:372, on a map mimic obtained inside object_from_map() (pager.c:284-305); all twelve writers of gy.youmonst.m_ap_type assign whole appearance values, so U_AP_TYPE's mask is defensive for the hero and never load-bearing. js/ has no writer of youmonst.m_ap_type at all. The finding also asserts that 'the same commit range added the const.js helper whose comment warns against exactly this read', but `git show aa9f3c85b1100bdb84517bf993ecceaf403c4eeb:js/const.js | grep -n 'M_AP_TYPE\b'` prints line 2878 defining M_AP_TYPE at the range base, and the range's only const.js change is the u_at() signature.  ||  causality refute: No behavior is introduced or exposed: the divergent stat Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: scripts/apply-stethoscope.test.mjs:310 (tests) — The `refreshes()` helper reports "no refresh happened" for any error other than `UnsupportedObjectOperationError`, so its two negative assertions pass whether the refresh was skipped or attempted and failed for an unrelated reason.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The collapsed catch can only hide an outcome if update_inventory() can fail with something other than UnsupportedObjectOperationError in this test's environment, and it cannot. Counter-evidence: js/invent.js:1018-1022 preflight_update_inventory() runs requireInventoryRefresh() first, and js/invent.js:1007-1013 throws UnsupportedObjectOperationError whenever program_state.in_moveloop is set, map output is not suppressed, iflags.perm_invent is true and hooks.updateInventory is absent — exactly the state the test installs at scripts/apply-stethoscope.test.mjs:301-303. Nothing past that point can run: line 1030 returns false when the hook is missing, so hooks.updateInventory() is never invoked and no TypeError can originate inside it. An implementation that wrongly refreshed on the floor object or on turn 1 would therefore throw precisely UnsupportedObjectOperationError, ref Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

passes.head: 049a95ae2bd0bb62fdbecd78c705d971059e6ff3
passes.evidence: Counts: 17 raw, 15 deduplicated, 14 confirmed, 14 applied, 0 deferred, 1 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 434 survivors of 507 mutants. Full correctness pass over the monsters deferral sweep and the first options slice. Four production defects, all applied. The sharpest was count_bind_keys(), which counted every BIND statement where C's cmdbind_add() overwrites in place: two binds of one key printed '(2 currently set)' against C's 1, reproduced and then pinned by a fresh three-segment differential whose bind-keys row now agrees with C. The other three shared one habit rather than being three slips: each justified a hard-coded answer by reasoning from the port's own parser gap as though it were evidence about C, so the fixes replace guesses with refusals and teach parseNethackrc() to record the statements it drops. One finding's preferred fix was declined as out of scope and applied as a refusal instead: routing applyBooleanOption()'s fallback through booleanOptionStorage() would activate about 47 options the parser currently drops, each with a live consumer, which is a state-owner change belonging to implementation. Applying the findings also corrected two of them: C's parsebindings() recurses into the comma suffix before handling the head, so the reviewer's second bind case was wrong, and optlist.h's negateok column makes sortloot's negation a stop rather than an ignored argument. Development score identical before and after at 1,043 of 7,765 screens and 116,207 of 610,816 PRNG values; suite 2,856 green. The mutation figure needs its recorded caveat: 425 of 434 survivors are in the generated table, which the runner does not exclude.

productionDefects.summary: js/cmd.js count_bind_keys() counted every `bind` operation, where C’s cmdbind_add() overwrites in place and keeps one entry per key, so two BIND statements for one key printed "(2 currently set)" against C’s "(1 currently set)". Both loops now read the createCommandBindingModel() bindings, which replay with C’s semantics, and the model gained C’s userbind flag. This also fixed the command(param) spelling, which was counted as zero.

js/options.js booleanOptionValue() read a boolean through allopt[].addr while applyBooleanOption()’s fallback wrote flags[<lowercased name>], so any boolean whose C storage name differs was read from the wrong place. Fixed by refusing when the two disagree, covering 32 divergent spellings. The finding’s preferred fix, routing the write through booleanOptionStorage(), was declined: it would activate about 47 options the parser currently drops, each with a live consumer, which is a state-owner change needing new end-to-end cases and therefore implementation rather than an audit fix.

js/options.js count_menucolors(), msgtype_count() and count_autocompletions() returned hard-coded answers justified by the port’s own parser gap rather than by C. parseNethackrc() now records a dropped MENUCOLOR, MSGTYPE or AUTOCOMPLETE statement with C’s own prefix lengths, and each count stops on its own statement instead of guessing.

js/options.js dosetEntryFormat() hard-coded doset()’s padded layout on a false premise, that menu_tab_sep is wizard-mode-only. set_wizonly governs where doset() lists an option, not whether a config file may set it, so the tab-separated form is reachable. Now refused by name, with the comment corrected.

mutation.finderConclusion: The headline survivor count is an artifact and must not be read as a coverage figure. 425 of the 434 survivors are in js/optlist_data.js, the generated options table: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs selects sites from changed lines and does not exclude declared generated outputs, so it mutated 217 table entries whose correctness comes from check:options diffing them against the C source rather than from any test. That also explains the boolean kind’s 16-of-442 figure. The real survivor list was nine, all outside the table, and it was routed to the tests finder, which traced each. The audit fixes killed eight; one remains, js/command_bindings.js setBinding()’s restBinding default, classified rather than fixed because no call omitting the argument can bind Space: extcmdlist has no row with key 0x20, the alias table has none, and resetCommandBindings() touches only direction keys and their variants. The tooling gap is worth recording separately, because every future goal that generates a table will bury its real survivors the same way.

passes.evidence: Counts: 18 raw, 14 deduplicated, 12 confirmed, 12 applied, 0 deferred, 1 rejected, 1 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 20 mutants. Full correctness pass over the twoweapon-command goal, closed over its own fixes. Its sharpest finding was against the goal record rather than the code: the boundary and detail cited dotwoweapon() as 845-905 and can_twoweapon() as 761-833, where the spans are 843-864 and 760-804. Line 905 is the head of untwoweapon(), so the bad span attributed untwoweapon() and drop_uswapwep() to this goal - the two functions its own open deferral records as unported, which a later selector would have read as done. The other production defects: the ADMITTED_COMMANDS comment named M-2 as the command's own key when its key is X and M-2 the alias; obj.h carried() became a sixth duplicate port and was converged; and two live fail-closed boundaries were unpinned, the newly reachable Dual-weps status field and both update_inventory() calls, the first now pinned by a fresh C recording rather than an assertion. Applying the findings corrected three of them, one materially: the reviewer justified an unreachable arm by saying no role starts with a launcher in a wield slot, but the human Ranger takes a dagger primary and a bow secondary; the arm is unreachable because wield.c:765 refuses that role monster one arm earlier, verified by replaying all thirteen roles. Score bit-identical per session at 1,081 of 7,765 screens and 116,787 of 610,816 PRNG values, which is the required outcome for a range no development session can reach; the evidence is the differential, now fourteen fresh C segments at 42,032 PRNG calls and 243 screens. Mutation was clean for the first time in this sequence - 20 of 20 killed, no generated-table noise - so the tests finder judged whether tests pin behavior instead of triaging survivors, which produced five of the twelve findings.

productionDefects.summary: The goal record’s own C citations were wrong, and the error was material. `boundary` and `detail` gave `dotwoweapon() (845-905)` and `can_twoweapon() (761-833)`; the spans are 843-864 and 760-804. Line 905 is the head of `untwoweapon()`, so the bad span attributed `untwoweapon()` and `drop_uswapwep()` to this goal — the two functions the open deferral `twoweapon-unreachable-refusal-arms` records as NOT ported. A later selector reading the boundary would have concluded they were done. Corrected in ce65d2f by direct edit, since goal-log.mjs offers no amend for an open goal’s boundary.

The ADMITTED_COMMANDS comment said `#twoweapon`’s "own key is M-2". Its own key is `X` (cmd.c:1913, extcmdlist row 0x58); M-2 is the alias commands_init() adds at cmd.c:2776, and the port binds both. A reader auditing the boundary would have concluded `X` was already handled.

`obj.h carried()` became a second live named port: `js/obj.js:675` exported, added by this range, beside the module-private `js/eat.js:598` with an identical body. The sixth duplicate port found in this repository in two days. Converged on js/obj.js, which obj.h names; js/eat.js repointed and the private copy deleted, with the development score verified bit-identical per session.

Two live fail-closed boundaries were unpinned: `set_twoweap(true, …)` makes js/display.js’s "Dual-weps" status field reachable for the first time, and both `update_inventory({ state })` calls in dotwoweapon() could be deleted with the whole suite still green, though under `OPTIONS=perm_invent` each is the port’s only stop. The status field was pinned by a new C recording rather than a unit assertion.

mutation.finderConclusion: The first clean mutation signal of this goal sequence: 20 of 20 killed, no survivors, no timeouts, and no declared generated output in range, so none of the distortion that made the three previous passes report 425, 827 and 826 meaningless survivors applies here. With no survivor list to triage, the tests finder was asked instead to sample-verify the claim that eighteen mutation-invisible lines had each been broken with their covering test observed to fail. That reframing produced five of the twelve findings, all of them gaps a survivor list could not have shown: an untested refusal-class registration, a matrix test re-asserting a constant copied from a few lines away, an unpinned `state.flags.female` guard, and a setuwep test covering three of its expression’s terms. The audit fixes added no mutable site of their own, so their evidence runs the other way: each new assertion was shown killing a specific mutant on already-committed lines.

readiness.boundary: The hero issues `#twoweapon`. On the success path the command prints "You begin two-weapon combat.", sets `u.twoweap`, refreshes inventory and spends or does not spend the move on one `rnd(20) > ACURR(A_DEX)`; on a refusal it prints one of seven messages and spends nothing. `seed0107-samurai-twoweapon-enhance` executes the success path in the running game, advancing from 15 to 40 of 98 screens.

The trace covered PRNG order: the command draws exactly one random number on the success path and none on any refusal, which the differential confirms.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Three arms stay unported with derivations recorded in code and tracked as `twoweapon-unreachable-refusal-arms`, and applying the findings corrected one of those derivations: the reviewer said no role starts with a launcher in a wield slot, but the human Ranger takes a dagger primary and a bow secondary (u_init.c:124-128). The arm is still unreachable, for the different reason that wield.c:765 refuses the Ranger and Caveman role monsters one arm earlier — verified by replaying all thirteen roles. passes.evidence: Counts: 21 raw, 20 deduplicated, 15 confirmed, 15 applied, 0 deferred, 5 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 11 mutants. Full correctness pass over three goals' work: chat-command, commands-deferral-sweep-2, and hero-combat slices 1 and 2. Four mandatory finders, 21 raw findings, 20 after deduplication, 15 confirmed by independent adversarial adjudication, 5 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. All 15 applied across five Audit-fix-for commits. Five were production defects, the sharpest being a refusal placed after a random-number draw and a state change in js/hack.js overexertion(), and an over-broad two-weapon refusal in js/uhitm.js do_attack() that was discarding three calls a turn from seed0107. Two findings were the eighth and ninth duplicate ports found in five days. Six were test defects, including a term whose deletion left all 3,000 tests green. Development score 1,102 of 7,765 screens and 116,830 of 610,816 calls, the only movement being seed0107 gaining the three calls the two-weapon refusal discarded.

productionDefects.summary: js/hack.js overexertion() refused both arms of hack.c overexert_hp() (3035-3047), where only the `uhp <= 1` arm prints, exercises Constitution and calls fall_asleep(). The `uhp > 1` arm is two portable statements. Worse, the refusal sat after gethungry() had spent rn2(20) and mutated u.uhunger, so a branch C walks past ended the segment after a draw and a state change. The common arm is now ported and only `uhp <= 1` refuses. Unreachable today through any admitted command, so it closed on authorized substituted evidence, tracked as overexertion-arm-has-no-fresh-differential.

js/uhitm.js do_attack() refused on u.twoweap alone, where uhitm.c:528 reaches unported code only when can_twoweapon() is additionally false. A two-weaponing hero walking into a hostile monster ended the segment three draws and one screen before C does. This is the only finding in the pass that moved the development score: seed0107-samurai-twoweapon-enhance gained the rn2(19), rnd(20) and rn2(3) the over-broad refusal discarded, 2842 to 2845 of 2902 calls, with every other session byte-identical.

js/uhitm.js attack_checks() read C’s Hallucination as intrinsic-or-extrinsic, dropping the !Halluc_resistance factor youprop.h:120 requires. That is a third distinct reading of one macro, in a file whose own is_safemon() 57 lines above reads it correctly. With hallucination intrinsic set and resistance active, C puts up the paranoid "Really attack?" prompt and the port did not. Reported independently by the correctness, readability and tests finders as findings 8, 9 and 12; one defect, fixed once.

display.h vobj_at() and engrave.c u_wipe_engr() each gained a second JavaScript home in this range: the new js/display.js vobj_at() against the pre-existing visibleObjectAt() at js/monmove.js, and the new js/engrave.js u_wipe_engr() against the statements inlined in js/allmain.js maybeWipeHeroEngraving(). The eighth and ninth duplicate ports found in five days. Both converged onto the file named for the C file, with the development score verified identical session by session across the convergence.

js/uhitm.js attack_checks() called engulfing_u(mtmp) against the module-global `game` while threading `state` through every other read in the same function, so a reader reasonably treating the function as state-pure would be wrong about its first guard.

mutation.finderConclusion: No survivors across the five audit-fix commits, but the number understates the work: two mutants survived the whole suite rather than one wave and needed new assertions written for them. js/monmove.js onscary()’s Elbereth disjunct had no test at all for its displaced-image and guarded-pile arms, and js/const.js engulfing_u()’s && survived flipping to || because nothing distinguished being held from being swallowed. The five test findings this pass confirmed are the same shape: finding 13 showed that deleting `!is_undead(mtmp.data)` from js/uhitm.js left all 3,000 tests green, and finding 15 that the known_hitum() test passed dieroll into the uattk slot, so it could not detect the parameter-order defect it existed to pin. Mutation score alone would have reported this range as healthy.

readiness.boundary: The range eed732b3..5168910 holds three goals: chat-command (sounds.c dotalk() and dochat() to the wall reply), commands-deferral-sweep-2 (hack.c end_running() and nomul() merged from two disagreeing ports into one, plus a fail-closed backstop at the two live domove() call sites), and hero-combat slices 1 and 2 (domove() reordered so the attack precedes test_move() as hack.c:2798 precedes 2843, then the hostile melee attempt ported down to the miss). The development score at the frozen head was 1,102 of 7,765 screens and 116,827 of 610,816 calls with 3 of 33 sessions matching; after the fixes it is 116,830, the whole movement in seed0107.
readiness.sourceReview: Four mandatory finders ran at full mode: correctness, readability-risk, test-quality and variable-flow. Neither optional finder was enabled, and both omissions were reasoned rather than skipped: the range adds no unbounded or amplified work, and source-required melee iteration does not trigger the performance finder on its own; the port is single-threaded replay, and although the reorder moved two awaits and the backstop added error handling around one, neither introduces overlapping work, cancellation or retries. Each finding was adversarially verified against the C source by an independent adjudicator applying evidence, causality and resolution checks; 15 of 20 deduplicated findings survived, 5 were rejected with counter-evidence, none went unverified and no warnings were raised. The random-number order of the melee path was re-derived from uhitm.c, eat.c and attrib.c rather than taken from the diff’s own comments, because the order originally supplied to the implementing agent was wrong.
readiness.completeness: All 15 confirmed findings are applied across five commits carrying Audit-fix-for: 5168910. Every new test was observed failing first by breaking the line it covers and restoring it, thirteen breakages in all, each named in its commit. Two items were reported rather than silently handled and are recorded in the ledger: overexertion-arm-has-no-fresh-differential, where no admitted command can raise the hero past Stressed encumbrance so the fresh differential AGENTS.md requires cannot be recorded yet and substituted evidence was authorized; and pickup-burden-option-has-no-parser, a live bug outside this range found while attempting that recording, where js/options.js has no parseoptions() arm for pickup_burden so the option silently becomes stricter than its default rather than looser. One trigger was deliberately not run: /simplify-codebase applies to artifact.c artifact_light()’s five ports, which is tracked as artifact-light-ported-five-times and scheduled into the slice that consumes the function.

Counter-evidence: The single live injection at js/hack.js:1780-1782 throws UnsupportedHeroMoveBoundaryError. passes.evidence: Counts: 17 raw, 17 deduplicated, 8 confirmed, 8 applied, 0 deferred, 9 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 60 survivors of 220 mutants. Full correctness pass over hero-combat slice 3, 1,439 changed production lines in one commit, plus the five audit-fix commits of the previous pass. Four mandatory finders; 17 raw, 17 deduplicated, 8 confirmed, 9 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. All 8 applied across two Audit-fix-for commits. No production behavior defect was confirmed, against five in the previous pass: the implementation held and the tests did not. Six of the eight were tests pinning nothing, each naming a term deletable with all 3,072 tests green, which matches the slice's own 68-of-144 mutation survivors. productionDefects.summary: js/uhitm.js hmon_hitmon() copied all 27 struct _hitmon_data fields, including doreturn and retval, while dropping C's guards that read them, so both fields were write-only. Harmless at the time because no ported helper sets them, and a time bomb for the slices that follow: artifact_hit() sets doreturn on DEADMONSTER(mon) to abort before damage lands, and the abort would have been discarded, subtracting damage from a monster already dead and then running _pet, _splitmon, _msg_hit and wakeup() on a corpse. The finding asked for three guards; the source gave one. C's guards at uhitm.c:1090-1091 and 1418-1419 are the last statements of their own functions, so the guarded return reaches exactly what the fall-through reaches, and both are no-ops in C. The guard at 1806-1807 was restored alone, with the other two documented as absent by derivation. Mutation confirms it is live: flipping the doreturn initializer to true now fails tests, where at dc31f03 it did not.

mutation.finderConclusion: The audit-fix diff itself holds no mutable site: 32 lines in scope, 0 sites, 0 mutants, because it is 26 comment lines plus one restored guard statement. The figure that matters is the before-and-after over js/uhitm.js at the same kinds: 220 mutants, 62 survivors at dc31f03 and 60 after, so two previously-surviving mutants became killable. One is the doreturn initializer, killed by the restored production guard; the other is the first && of uhitm.c:1467's condition, killed by the new two-handed strength test, where JavaScript precedence turns a && b && c into a || (b && c) and the one-handed row lands two points where it expects one. The other five test findings kill nothing, and that is structural rather than a shortfall: they name term deletions, while the mutator's site set is operators and literals, so dropping a whole disjunct is outside what it can express. That is the same gap the previous pass demonstrated from the other direction, where a range scored 253 of 220 mutants killed while six real test defects sat in it. The 60 remaining first-wave survivors cluster in the _hitmon_data initializers, the first_weapon_hit() guard whose body is empty so nothing it decides is observable, and mhitm_knockback()'s return statements whose value hmon_hitmon discards; most look structurally unkillable, and recording that here should spare the next pass re-deriving it.

It could not fire today, because PIT sits in UNPORTED_TRAP_EFFECTS, but it would have become a live wrong stop the moment mintrap()'s pit arm landed, aborting a segment on an ordinary early-level kill that C completes. A test at scripts/mon-kill.test.mjs pinned the wider behavior, so the defect was held in place by its own coverage. Applying it corrected both findings that reported it, which proposed contradictory fixes: neither arm needs an unported operation, so both flags are ported and xkilled() gains no refusal. The flags remain unreachable, but for a reason neither finding gave -- mondead() stops on both boulder states before xkilled() reads either, at fill_pit()'s settling refusal and flooreffects()'s boulder-landing refusal, and both stops sit above the rn2(6) treasure draw.

passes.evidence: Counts: 17 raw, 15 deduplicated, 13 confirmed, 13 applied, 0 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 1 mutants. Full correctness pass over the enhance-command goal and two trap-activation slices. Four mandatory finders; 17 raw, 15 deduplicated, 13 confirmed, 2 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. All 13 applied across four Audit-fix-for commits, score unchanged. Two production defects: nh_timeout()'s invulnerability guard was missing from the live path, and the movement seam still screened a destination square on the assumption that u.utrap could not be set for the hero, which this range made false. Six were tests, the fourth consecutive pass where tests lead. The sharpest showed map_trap() had no oracle of any kind, its whole body replaceable with an early return while both the 3,162-test suite and the development score stayed identical session by session. Applying the findings corrected two against source and found a defect in a third's proposed test.

productionDefects.summary: js/timeout.js nh_timeout_elapsed_turn() ran the property countdown unconditionally, after the preflight had already returned early for an invulnerable hero, so C's if (u.uinvulnerable) return; at timeout.c:621-622 was missing from the live path. The guard is now where C has it, between adjust_timeout_luck() and decrement_property_timeouts(). Applying it corrected the finding's companion: the pass also proposed dropping the preflight's copy of the same guard, which would have been wrong, because everything the preflight validates sits below C's return -- the mtimedone, ucreamed, usptime and ugallop arms at 641-667, the countdown at 670-671, and run_timers() at 947 -- so removing it would refuse state C never reads. Unreachable in a scored session today because prayer is unported and nothing in js/ writes u.uinvulnerable.

u.utrap became settable for the hero for the first time in this range, and the movement admission seam ahead of domove() still screened the destination square on the old assumption that it could not be set. That is a live divergence rather than a stale guard: hack.c:2830 precedes test_move() at 2843, and trapmove()'s TT_BEARTRAP arm always falls through to return FALSE at 1690, so C never reads the destination for a bear trap. The fix guards on the trap type rather than on u.utrap, because TT_PIT returns TRUE at 1583 and TT_BURIEDBALL at 1648 and both do reach test_move(). It was reachable from the committed recipe: two existing matrix levels already place a refused square beside their trap, a closed door on seed 69 and an unported trap type on seed 395.

mutation.finderConclusion: The audit-fix diff held exactly one mutable site across seven js/ files and 79 lines in scope, the && in the new heldStepIgnoresDestination(), which survived until the TT_BURIEDBALL case was added and is killed now. The figure is uninformative on its own and the pass's own evidence explains why: finding 1 showed map_trap()'s entire body could be replaced with an early return while the 3,162-test suite and the development score both stayed identical, session by session, and the slice that introduced it had run only boolean, logical and relational kinds, under which a statement deletion has no site at all. Three instruments were blind to the same function. That is the fourth consecutive pass in which the mutation figure and the test quality point in different directions, and this time the deletion was invisible to the score as well.

readiness.sourceReview: Four mandatory finders at full mode. Neither optional finder ran; the range adds no unbounded work and the port is single-threaded replay. Every finding was adversarially verified against C by an independent adjudicator: 13 of 15 survived, 2 were rejected with counter-evidence, none went unverified and no warnings were raised. This range was briefed asymmetrically because it retires a blanket refusal on any trap square and replaces it with dotrap()'s dispatcher, which newly makes the opposite failure possible -- an arm narrower than C admitting an unported trap type silently, which AGENTS.md forbids where a spurious stop is merely permitted. Both directions were checked. Applying the findings corrected two of them against the source, and found a defect in a third's proposed test: asserting the encumbrance line does not kill deleting encumber_msg() from set_wounded_legs(), because allmain.c:208 opens the next turn with an identical call, so a direct call isolating do.c:2445 was written instead.
readiness.completeness: All 13 confirmed findings are applied across four commits carrying Audit-fix-for: 533ac18. Six were tests, the fourth consecutive pass in which tests are the largest category: 24 of 47 findings across the four. The sharpest was map_trap(), a newly ported function with no oracle of any kind -- its whole body could be replaced with an early return and both the test suite and the development score stayed identical. Every new assertion was observed failing first by breaking the term it covers and restoring it, including four printed lines deleted or reindexed, the rn2(2) leg arms swapped, rn1(10,10) perturbed in both directions, is_whirly() dropped, and map_trap()'s body stubbed with each guard inverted. Two limits are recorded rather than papered over: the leg-side ternary has no RIGHT_SIDE case because all seven matrix segments draw rn2(2)=0 and a second bite kills the fixture, and map_trap()'s glyph assertion is partly self-referential and would not catch a wrong TRAP_COLORS entry, though its two guards and the trap-argument drop are genuine oracles. The fresh differential grew to seven segments, 21,588 calls, 80 screens and 80 cursors, all matching.

passes.evidence: Counts: 20 raw, 17 deduplicated, 12 confirmed, 12 applied, 0 deferred, 5 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 1 survivors of 10 mutants. Full correctness pass over trap-activation's last slice and the whole armor-takeoff goal. Four mandatory finders; 20 raw, 17 deduplicated, 12 confirmed, 5 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. All 12 applied across four Audit-fix-for commits, score identical per session. Both refusal directions produced a confirmed finding: heldStepIgnoresDestination() was narrower than C and skipped preflight_dotrap(), and mintrap()'s tail was wider than C and cost real screens on fresh cases (3 of 41 to 41/41 on one recorded seed). Two more duplicate ports, eleven and twelve. Five were tests, including an assert.rejects() that passed by catching the harness's own queue-empty error rather than any game result.

productionDefects.summary: heldStepIgnoresDestination(), added by the previous pass_s own audit fix, skipped the whole destination chain including preflight_dotrap(). That is the narrower-than-C direction, which AGENTS.md forbids while merely permitting a spurious stop. hack.c domove_core():2822-2825 runs avoid_trap_andor_region() above the u.utrap block at 2830, so it is the one call that reads a held hero_s destination: its second arm prompts on a tseen trap, its first on a visible region, and options.c:7173 sets PARANOID_TRAP by default. The arm now refuses those two destinations and the terrain bypass stands. This is the second consecutive pass to find a defect in the previous pass_s fix, which is the case for leaving audit-fix commits outside the frontier.

trapeffect_pit()_s new mtmp.mtrapped = true made mintrap()_s tail refusal reachable, and that refusal was far wider than the C block it stands for: maybe_unhide_at() calls hideunder() only under if (undetected && ...), and canspotmon() = canseemon() || sensemon() makes the !alreadyspotted && canseemon() arm unreachable, so trap.c:3827-3835 is a no-op for a monster that was not hiding. The fifth refusal wider than C confirmed in this port. It was invisible to the development set and materially wrong on fresh cases: scanning 6,600 segments for a monster surviving a pit found five, and the two recorded went from 3 of 41 screens to 41/41 and from 6 of 8 to 8/8.

save_mtraits() deep-copied mtrack but left mgoal aliased, where C_s *mtmp2 = *mtmp at mkobj.c:2167 and the memcpy at mkobj.c:430 copy the whole struct by value and monst.h:189 declares mgoal a coord value member. The corpse_s saved traits are meant to be a frozen snapshot and shared one coord object with the live monster. The port already knew the rule fifty lines away, at js/unported_monster_actions.js:276. Fixed in both homes, including js/obj.js copy_oextra() which sits outside the reviewed range, because leaving one half is how this class persists.

dungeon.c has_ceiling() became the eleventh duplicate port found in eight days, against the pre-existing currentLevelHasCeiling() at js/monmove.js:708. Converging it was behavior-preserving only after has_ceiling() was state-scoped: the deleted currentLevelHasCeiling() read state.astral_level and state.earth_level while the new has_ceiling() read the game singleton through js/const.js, so applying the convergence alone would have regressed m_in_air(). The two landed together.

mon.c copy_mextra() became the twelfth duplicate port: js/obj.js copy_oextra() still open-coded the same C call as structuredClone(sourceMonster.mextra) after copy_mextra() was ported to own it. Converged onto the file mon.c names, with the development score verified identical session by session.

mutation.finderConclusion: Ten mutants over the audit-fix diff at all four kinds, nine killed. The survivor is js/trap_effects.js:890, integer 1 to 0 on monster.mhp >= 1, which differs only for a monster with no hit points left; m_detach() clears mundetected for every monster it removes from the map, so nothing reaches that line with mhp 0, mtrapped and mundetected together. The relational mutant on the same line was killed by setting the fixture_s hit points so rnd(6) leaves exactly 1. The more telling number is not the ratio but finding 12: an assert.rejects() with no error matcher was passing because it caught the harness_s Input queue empty error rather than any game result, which no mutation kind can express.

rejections.summary: js/corpstat.js:71 — save_mtraits()'s comment presents mtrack as the one nested value the shallow spread has to copy by hand, but newMonster() also gives every monster `mgoal: { x, y }`, which the spread aliases into the saved traits.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: The distinctive readability claim is not what the source says, and the residual defect is index 0's. Counter-evidence: The comment at js/corpstat.js:71-74 reads: "C's `*mtmp2 = *mtmp` copies the struct by value, so the fixed-size mtrack array inside it is copied too; js/obj.js copy_oextra() maps the same array for the same reason." It explains one deep copy and nowhere claims to enumerate every by-value member, so the premise that it "reads as a completed audit of which struct-monst members ... copies by value" is the finding's inference, not a statement in the file. Stripped of that inference, the finding is the same one-line code defect already reported at index 0, with the same anchor (js/corpstat.js:71) and the same fix, and adds no impact beyond it.  ||  resolution refute: Both branches of the proposed fix either duplicate index 0 or move the problem into prose. rejections.summary: js/do_wear.js:437 — do_wear.js reads the armor-category field as `oc_subtyp` in all four places, where C and every other file in js/ spell it `oc_armcat`; the comment at 436-438 compounds this by asserting that js/obj.js is_shield() reads the same `oc_subtyp` alias, which it does not.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The compound claim does not survive reading the comment and its siblings. Counter-evidence: The comment at js/do_wear.js:436-438 reads "C ref: obj.h is_boots() (285-287) and is_gloves() (288-290), beside js/obj.js is_shield(). Both read the objects[] field stored here under its oc_subtyp union alias." The subject of "Both" is the two functions the first sentence names and the file then defines — is_boots() and is_gloves() — not is_shield(); the finding's central assertion, that the comment "asserts that js/obj.js is_shield() reads the same oc_subtyp alias", rests on the less natural reading. The claim of a broken sibling convention also fails: js/obj.js itself reads the union under both spellings, deliberately and with comments saying so — js/obj.js:717 ("oc_armcat is the objects[] field's armor-category alias, over the same storage is_ammo() above reads as oc_subtyp") a Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: js/do_wear.js:439 — is_boots() and is_gloves() are defined here, while their obj.h sibling is_shield() lives in js/obj.js:718 and the same three predicates are also inlined in js/objnam.js — a third home for one small group of C macros, and the new pair already disagrees with js/obj.js on the field spelling.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: The 'third home' is pre-existing and untouched, and the drift the finding points at is not drift. Counter-evidence: `git diff --stat 533ac18..54b3400 -- js/objnam.js js/obj.js` returns nothing: neither file is modified anywhere in the reviewed range, so js/objnam.js:328-330's open-coding and js/obj.js's ownership of is_shield both predate it. What the range adds is the first and only definition of is_boots() and is_gloves() in the port, placed next to their sole caller, cursed() at js/do_wear.js:415-416 — that is a file-placement judgement, not a duplicate port, and the brief reserves structural relocation for the simplification pass. The claimed "divergence has already begun" is two spellings of one accessor: js/objects.js:1544-1553 aliases oc_armcat to oc_subtyp, so js/obj.js:721 and js/do_wear.js:441 read the same storage and return the same value.  ||  resolution re Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: js/do_wear.js:636 — ParanoidRemove() hides an options-parsing refusal behind flag.h's boolean macro name, re-encodes a rule js/options.js already owns and pins with a test, and its comment says optfn_paranoid_confirmation() is unported when js/options.js:2968 ports that function's get_val arm.

passes.evidence: Counts: 16 raw, 16 deduplicated, 9 confirmed, 9 applied, 0 deferred, 7 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 2 mutants. Full correctness pass over the drop-command goal, three scripts-only tooling changes, and the reachable-refusal-escapes goal. Four mandatory finders; 16 raw, 16 deduplicated, 9 confirmed, 7 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. All 9 applied across three Audit-fix-for commits with the score unchanged per session. One production defect: the merge admission guarded the object being dropped where merged() reads the floor pile member it absorbs, proven by execution rather than argument, and the same mid-transaction failure the drop slice had been written to close. Five were tests, the sixth consecutive pass where tests lead or tie. Two of the nine were defects in work this session produced, making this the third consecutive pass to find a defect in the previous round's fix.

productionDefects.summary: The merge admission in preflight_dropx() tested lamplit, timed and globby on the object being dropped, while invent.c merged() reads those fields on the floor pile member it absorbs. mergable() forces lamplit to match and short-circuits on globby, so two of the three were accidentally symmetric; timed was not, because mergable() rejects a timer mismatch only for EGG and revivable CORPSE. The finder proved it by execution rather than argument: the object left inventory, place_object() ran, and only then did UnsupportedObjectOperationError fire. That is the same mid-transaction failure the drop slice had been written to close, still open one level down. It was unreachable from a d keystroke because drop() refuses every CORPSE, so the invariant was broken while the score was not. The orchestrator recommended the fix that supplies the missing operations from objectGenerationHooks(); that rested on a false premise, since it supplies stopObjectTimers but neither mergeLightSources nor absorbGlob, both of which are unported C in light.c and mkobj.c. The applied fix walks the floor pile and refuses any member mergable() would accept that carries one of the three fields, which also covers the wish path in js/zap.js because it shares the admission.

mutation.finderConclusion: Two mutants over the js/ diff, both on the new pile-walk guard, both killed. The number is small because two of the three commits are scripts/-only, which the mutator does not scope. The more useful measurement was made by hand: deleting both halves of the merge admission and running the full suite gives 3270 pass and 1 fail, and the single failure is the new merge test, so that test is the sole cover for the invariant. The commit body had recorded this more weakly from a single-line deletion, and the stronger uniqueness claim is verified here rather than there.

passes.evidence: Counts: 21 raw, 16 deduplicated, 13 confirmed, 13 applied, 0 deferred, 3 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 4 survivors of 36 mutants. Full correctness pass over the pickup-command goal: the , command for a square holding at most one takeable object. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered, since the range adds only source-required iteration and no shared-state or overlapping-lifecycle change. The finding that mattered is the burden gate: the , command routed through a limit computed with Math.max(near_capacity(), flags.pickup_burden), and an rc file leaves that option as raw text, so the limit was NaN and the refusal silently disappeared rather than widening. It was reachable only through an option no scored session sets, which is why two slices, a mutation run and 17 recorded C segments all passed over it, and why the variable-trace finder rather than the score found it. Tests led again: 5 of 13 confirmed were test gaps, the seventh consecutive pass where tests lead or tie. Three of those gaps sat in work this session produced, including nine recorded segments that npm test never replayed. The score is unchanged at 1254 screens and 117940 calls across the fixes, as a set that changes no scored behavior should be. The pass also opened one new ledger entry, addinv-burden-read-accepts-unparsed-option, for the same read one level down in js/invent.js, which is outside this range.

productionDefects.summary: preflightPickupObjects() in js/pickup.js computed its burden limit as Math.max(near_capacity(), flags.pickup_burden ?? MOD_ENCUMBER), the gate the `,` command newly routes through. parseNethackrc() has no arm for pickup_burden and keeps an unported option's raw text in flags[<option name>], which for this option is the field the parsed value would occupy, so OPTIONS=pickup_burden:overloaded leaves a string there. Math.max() then returns NaN and calc_capacity(...) > NaN is false for every value, so the refusal disappeared rather than widening: the port lifted the object where pickup.c:1759-1777 stops at a ynq() prompt. Fail-open, and invisible to the development score because no scored session sets the option. Fixed with a Number.isInteger() guard that refuses an unusable value before the limit is computed, keeping the boundary closed until js/options.js gains the parse arm. js/invent.js addinvCore1() holds the same read one level down, where the string makes a comparison false rather than deleting a refusal; that file is outside this range and is recorded as the deferral addinv-burden-read-accepts-unparsed-option.

Stone_resistance had two differently-written owners once this range added the second. js/pickup.js u_safe_from_fatal_corpse()'s st_resists arm reads the macro as (intrinsic || extrinsic), while js/invent.js activeStoneResistance(), read by will_feel_cockatrice(), added a `&& !blocked` term. youprop.h:65 defines Stone_resistance as (HStone_resistance || EStone_resistance) and carries no blocked term, unlike Blind() at :103 which does, so the invent.js copy was the wrong one. Renamed to Stone_resistance for the macro it ports and the term dropped. No behavior moved: nothing in js/ writes uprops[STONE_RES].blocked, and the development score is identical. The finder proposed one shared owner called from both files; the narrower fix was applied instead, because a per-file local property reader is the established idiom here -- a dozen files carry their own propertyActive() -- and the defect was the divergence, not the two call sites.

rejections.summary: A correctness finding that js/hack.js:2154's `if (ret >= 0)` is unpinned and its surviving mutant semantically inequivalent, filed as a correctness defect.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator refuted the category, not the observation: js/hack.js:2154 reproduces hack.c:3884 `if ((ret = pickup_checks()) >= 0) return ret ? ECMD_TIME : ECMD_OK;` exactly, and the shipped code answers C's result on both squares the finding named. The only substantiated problem is absent test coverage, which the confirmed test-category finding at the same site reports; filing it twice double-counts one gap. The coverage gap was fixed. Do not reopen as a correctness defect without a source divergence in the shipped line, as opposed to a missing test.

rejections.summary: A readability finding that preflightPickupObjects()'s header overclaims by saying it holds everything C decides inside pickup_object(), lift_object(), pick_obj() and addinv() that can refuse, while shop billing is refused elsewhere.
rejections.counterEvidence: pickup.c:1893-1941 pick_obj() contains no refusal at all: it computes robshop, calls addtobill() and remote_burglary(), and always returns addinv()'s result. There is therefore nothing C decides in pick_obj() that can refuse for the header to be missing. The port's shop stop is a port-side inability to bill, not a C decision, so the premise that one C refusal is handled in two places does not hold. Do not reopen without naming an early return or refusal inside pick_obj() in the C source.

rejections.summary: A readability finding that pickup()'s header misleads by saying every square with a second object stops before ownership changes, while the same paragraph documents autopick() lifting whole multi-object piles.
rejections.counterEvidence: The sentence immediately before the limits list (js/pickup.js) already scopes the two arms by name -- autopick()'s, used by a level teleport arrival, and the `,` command's, for a square holding exactly one object it is allowed to take -- so the one-object restriction is attributed to `,` one line above. The list reads as the union of pickup()'s refusals, and other items in it are equally arm-specific in the opposite direction. Do not reopen without a reading that survives the preceding sentence.

mutation.deltaRun: 2 mutants, 0 survivors over the audit-fix diff
mutation.finderConclusion: The tests finder traced all four survivors. It confirmed the slice worker's classification of three of them -- js/pickup.js:595, :744 and :746, all one branch in pickup_object()'s corpse arm -- because preflightPickupObjects() refuses every corpse for which fatal_corpse_mistake() or rider_corpse_revival() would answer TRUE, so both answer FALSE for every object reaching the loop and pickup_object() returns 1 on every path. The fourth, js/hack.js:2154, was unclassified and turned out to be a real gap: it survived because on an empty square pickup() also answers 0, so `>=` and `>` agree there. A new test drives dopickup() on an empty square with MENU_TRADITIONAL, where pickup() refuses and the two spellings differ, and it kills the mutant. Three further gaps the mutation run could not see were found by reading: the nine recorded empty-square segments had no replay in npm test, preflight_dropx()'s new mergable() conjunct had no negative row, and the autopickup corpse arm this range made live had no test at all.

readiness.boundary: Starting event: the `,` keystroke, or `#pickup` typed at the extended-command prompt. Ending events: the terrain message pickup_checks() prints for a square with nothing to take, with no turn spent; or the `<letter> - <object>` line pickup_prinv() prints for the one object the square held, with one turn spent. The real game executes both, confirmed by nine and eight recorded C segments replayed by the port (25,371 and 22,182 PRNG calls, 102 screens and 102 cursors in total), and by three development sessions that walked past the keystroke they previously stopped on.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable before the ending events was traced against nethack-c/upstream/: hack.c pickup_checks() (3788-3871) and dopickup() (3876-3891); pickup.c pickup() (672-910), query_objlist()'s counting loop and both early returns (1046-1077), all_but_uchain() (508-512), pickup_object() (1803-1888), u_safe_from_fatal_corpse() (272-284), fatal_corpse_mistake() (285-302) and rider_corpse_revival() (303-316). The trace covered state, PRNG order and the points where the game waits for input. Stubs and explicit stops were identified and are listed under completeness. Two source-fidelity errors the trace caught are recorded above: the Stone_resistance divergence, and a FOLLOW() citation naming hack.h:1243, which is the BY_NEXTHERE bit, rather than pickup.c:56-58. A third, in the goal's own forecast witness, attributed u_safe_from_fatal_corpse()'s answer for a Monk to the st_petrifies term when u_init.c:101-102 makes the st_gloves term answer first; it was corrected in commit c3e5435 before the pass ran.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Every reachable excluded branch refuses before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output, which the pass checked explicitly because a previous pass in this repository found a refusal that fired mid-transaction. Excluded and verified fail-closed: two or more allowed objects, which fall past pickup.c:1077 into sortloot() and create_nhwindow(); MENU_TRADITIONAL; a nonzero count, which `m1,` proves reachable and which the `what < 0` arm refuses; u.uswallow and pickup_checks()'s pool, lava and can_reach_floor() arms; pickup_object()'s OBJ_MINVENT, oartifact and SCR_SCARE_MONSTER arms; fatal_corpse_mistake()'s petrifying branch and rider_corpse_revival()'s revive_corpse(); shop squares, where costly_spot() would bill through pick_obj(); and, added by this pass, an unparsed pickup_burden. The two-object case is pinned by a differential matching all 2,881 PRNG calls and every screen before the keystroke, with no frame drawn for the command.

passes.evidence: Counts: 15 raw, 14 deduplicated, 11 confirmed, 10 applied, 1 deferred, 3 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 3 survivors of 34 mutants. Full correctness pass over the two force-fight-command slices. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered, since the range adds no hot-path or resource cost and no overlapping-lifecycle work. The pass earned its place on risk rather than size: 483 changed lines, but they replaced a single-prefix arm with a general prefix loop, corrected three lines that had been latently wrong for as long as nothing set context.forcefight, and made a representation decision outside C. Two production defects were applied and one deferred, and the first applied one was introduced by the range itself: moving unmap_object() back to C's position put a refusal below it, so a stop fired after map memory and the display buffer had been rewritten. That is the same late-refusal failure mode an earlier pass in this repository found, arriving by a different route -- an ordering fix that was right for the arms C completes and wrong for the one the port refuses. The second, a bare Error in unmap_invisible(), would have escaped the segment rather than ending it, and its stated reason had been falsified by this very range porting unmap_object(). Tests led again: 5 of 11 confirmed were test gaps, the eighth consecutive pass where tests lead or tie, and four of the five were invisible to the mutation run because they sit on ordering or on lines with no mutable site. One further gap the pass created rather than found is recorded separately as parsed-retry-forcefight-restore-untested. The score is unchanged at 1294 screens and 118144 calls across the fixes.

productionDefects.summary: js/hack.js domove_fight_empty() refused terrain with no remembered appearance after unmap_object() and newsym() had already run. Slice 2 introduced this by moving unmap_object() back to C's position (hack.c:2280-2285) without noticing that C's seenv test at 2302 sits below it because C completes that arm rather than refusing it. The port refuses, so putting the refusal where C puts the test meant a stop that had rewritten map memory and the display buffer, ending the segment on a screen the port had already diverged from -- the late-refusal failure mode this repository has found before. Fixed by hoisting the seenv/IS_STWALL/SDOOR/SCORR test above unmap_object(), guarded by the already-computed `solid`, with a comment stating that this is the one place the port deliberately departs from C's order and only on the arm it refuses. Pinned by asserting that the square's remembered_glyph and the top line are both untouched after the refusal.

js/display.js unmap_invisible() refused with a bare Error whose stated reason was that unmap_object() is not ported. This range ported unmap_object(), so the reason had ceased to exist, and a bare Error is not one of the classes js/cmd.js failClosedCommandRefusals() converts, so it would have escaped the segment as a hard failure and discarded the matching prefix instead of ending on it. Fixed by raising UnsupportedMapMemoryError and naming the blocker that actually remains: map_invisible(), the only writer of the 'I' marker the arm clears, is unported, so the arm has never run. The TRUE arm was deliberately left unwritten rather than implemented, because AGENTS.md forbids preparing an unreachable branch. js/detect.js:624's comment carried the same falsified claim and was corrected. An existing test in scripts/detect.test.mjs pinned the old message and was updated.

js/cmd.js captureParsedCommand() recorded the reqmenu prefix's effect (iflags.menu_requested) but not the fight prefix's (context.forcefight), so a retryable boundary raised under a force-fight would replay the direction key as a plain walk -- a different command from the one the player typed -- and would leave the flag set into the following command. The capture site at js/cmd.js inside rhack()'s prefix loop runs after do_fight() has set the flag, so the path is reachable. Fixed by capturing and restoring it alongside menuRequested, with the doc comment rewritten to name both prefixes. The new property's boolean mutant survives the suite because no test drives a retry through that path; that is a coverage gap rather than an unkillable mutant, and it is recorded as the deferral parsed-retry-forcefight-restore-untested.

js/hack.js domove_fight_empty()'s dig-tool guard refuses every force-fight by a hero wielding a pick or an axe, which is dig.c:173 dig_typ()'s own first test and no more. C refuses only when dig_typ() answers something other than DIGTYP_UNDIGGABLE: dig.c:176-179 gives an axe DIGTYP_UNDIGGABLE at every wall, rock, pool and furniture square, where C swings and spends the turn, and dig.c:181-191 gives a pick DIGTYP_UNDIGGABLE on ROOM and CORR. scripts/force-fight.test.mjs's PICK_AXE/AXE row at a VWALL was pinning the port's refusal as though it were C's behavior. The guard is fail-closed, so the port is narrower than C rather than wrong. Narrowing it would make an axe-wielding hero's swing at a wall live, which is new supported behavior needing its own recorded C differential, so under .agents/review.md that returns to implementation rather than being an audit fix. Deferred as dig-tool-guard-refuses-where-dig_typ-answers-undiggable; the guard's comment and the test's comment now both state the real width.

rejections.summary: A correctness finding that executeMovement() still passes the command row's run value to preflightDomoveDestination(), the same wrong source corrected six lines below, so under a prefix that pre-commits DOMOVE_WALK the admission seam branches on a run value set_move_cmd() will never install.
rejections.counterEvidence: The deviation is provably unobservable rather than merely masked. A forcefight with a nonzero run value is reachable only through a prefix pair, because the runwest/runeast rows carry MOVEMENTCMD|CMD_M_PREFIX and no CMD_gGF_PREFIX (js/extcmdlist_data.js:199-206), so `FL` is refused at the prefix flag test and only `mFL`/`FmL` with wasMPrefix latched get through. In every such case iflags.menu_requested is true, which sends requireNoMonsterBump() down the same arm regardless of the run value. Do not reopen without an input that reaches preflightDomoveDestination() with a nonzero run value and menu_requested false.

rejections.summary: A readability finding that rhack()'s prologue comment claims C resets both prefix effects at every rhack() entry, while the fight prefix's effect, context.forcefight, is deliberately not reset there.
rejections.counterEvidence: The comment is accurate as written. The two statements it introduces are `state.iflags.menu_requested = false;` and `state.context.nopick = 0;` -- exactly the two values cmd.c:3634-3636 resets in rhack()'s prologue, and exactly the two effects the `m` prefix leaves behind. It says 'both prefix effects', not 'both prefixes'. Do not reopen without showing that C resets a third value there.

rejections.summary: A readability finding that glyph_to_cmap() carries C's name and a C-shaped docstring but accepts only a record terrainCmap() built moments earlier, so map-memory and display-buffer records lack the cmap property and make it throw a bare TypeError.
rejections.counterEvidence: No current caller misuses the function, and the behavior follows the file's established convention rather than introducing a new hazard: show_glyph_cell() and remembered_glyph_from_presentation() each throw an equally unlisted bare TypeError for a wrong-shaped presentation record, so an escaping TypeError on a programming error is how this module already signals one. Do not reopen without a caller that reaches it with a record lacking the property.

The guard is fail-closed, so the port is narrower than C rather than wrong. mutation.deltaRun: 5 mutants, 1 survivor over the audit-fix diff; the survivor is the new forcefight property in captureParsedCommand(), deferred as parsed-retry-forcefight-restore-untested
mutation.finderConclusion: The tests finder traced all three window survivors and confirmed the slice worker's classification of each: js/cmd.js's `iflags.menu_requested = false` write, which rhack() clears at every entry (cmd.c:3609) above both readers, and the two '<'/'>' disjunctions at js/cmd.js:1520-1521, where no extcmdlist row makes one conjunct true and the other false. It then found four gaps the mutation run could not see, because they sit on lines with no mutable site or on ordering rather than operators: the executeMovement() correction reading domoveAttempting was unpinned and reverting it left the whole suite green while `mFL` diverges; `prefixSeen = command` was unpinned and a first-wins latch left the suite green while changing what `Fmi` and `mFi` print; the uhitm.c:462 forcefight conjunct in requireSupportedDestinationMonster() had no test at all; and the engraved-square test asserted only the error class, so the unmap_object() hoist the second slice exists to make was not pinned. The dark-room test also varied only waslit and never the terrain, leaving the `typ === ROOM` conjunct with no negative case. All five now have tests, each observed failing first.

readiness.boundary: Starting event: the `F` key, or `-`, followed by a movement command; also `m` in either order with it. Ending events: the swing message domove_fight_empty() prints for the square attacked -- "You harmlessly attack the wall." for solid terrain, "You attack thin air." for anything accessible and not furniture -- with one turn spent; or, for a prefix followed by a command that does not accept it, cmd.c rhack()'s refusal line with no turn spent. The real game executes all of these: twelve recorded C segments replayed by the port over 31,346 PRNG calls and 56 screens, and seed0013-rogue-friday13-combat now matches completely at 59/59 steps and 4838/4838 calls.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable before the ending events was traced against nethack-c/upstream/: cmd.c do_fight() (1621-1634) and rhack()'s PREFIXCMD/MOVEMENTCMD tail (3693-3800); hack.c domove_fight_empty() (2227-2338), move_out_of_bounds() (2585-2610) and domove_core()'s 2805-2810 block; display.c unmap_object() and map_background(); and the reads in dig.c dig_typ() (168-192) and uhitm.c (201, 462) that decide two of the arms. The trace covered state, PRNG order and the points where the game waits for input. It found four source-fidelity errors, all recorded above or in the range's own commits: the late refusal, the bare Error, the dig-guard width, and the missing forcefight capture. passes.head: 6b87d14d284275e4c39c9f02858dfbafc4c5754b
passes.evidence: Counts: 13 raw, 13 deduplicated, 9 confirmed, 8 applied, 1 deferred, 4 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 0 mutants. Full correctness pass over the commands deferral sweep: five ledger entries, four of which changed production code. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered, since the range adds no hot-path cost and no overlapping-lifecycle work. No production defect was found, which for a sweep is the expected result and is consistent with a range mutation run that produced no mutants at all. That empty run is the pass's most useful methodological result: the changed lines hold almost no relational, logical or boolean sites -- a bare return false, an assignment and a call, a straight-line body -- so the zero carries no evidence either way rather than evidence of coverage, and the three gaps it could not see were all found by reading. The one production change hardens an implicit contract whose two failure modes run in opposite directions: stop_occupation() took an optional env while env.message was mandatory on its common arm, where a missing operation is a bare TypeError that js/jsmain.js does not convert, so the segment is discarded rather than ended; on the sibling arm the same omission silently falls through to the live terminal writer during a planning clone. Five of the nine confirmed findings were comments the range itself falsified, which is now the third consecutive pass to find that pattern and the strongest recurring signal in this ledger. Tests led or tied for the ninth consecutive pass. One finding is deferred with its test shape and required mutation recorded.

productionDefects.summary: js/allmain.js stop_occupation() took `env = {}` while env.message is mandatory on its common arm, and the header described env only as something maybe_finished_meal() forwards to eatfood(), never as an operation this function calls itself. The two ways of getting it wrong fail in opposite directions, which is why the implicit contract was worth hardening rather than documenting: on the printing arm a missing message is a bare TypeError, and js/jsmain.js breaks the segment only for the named boundary classes, so the whole segment is discarded rather than ended on its last matching screen; on the finished-meal arm the same omission is not fatal at all, because js/eat.js eatOperations() defaults `message = ttyPline`, so a planning-mode caller that forgot it would write to the live terminal during a dry run. Reproduced by execution: calling stop_occupation with an installed occupation and `{ statusRefresh }` alone throws `TypeError: env.message is not a function`, and that shape is not hypothetical -- js/allmain.js invokes the occupation callback with exactly `{ statusRefresh }` twenty lines above the new call site. The range multiplied the caller count from one unexported helper to three exported call sites, and C has roughly fifteen further stop_occupation() sites unported, so new callers are expected. Fixed by resolving message through a requireOccupationOperation() helper matching the requireEatOperation/requireAttackOperation/requireDochugwOperation idiom the same file family already uses, and by rewriting the header to say message is required whenever an occupation is installed.

rejections.summary: A finding that js/hack.js's rewritten comment says the fight prefix swings at the pet while the code four lines later routes that pet through a helper named requireOrdinaryHostileMelee, so the name contradicts the prose.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator found the naming consistent with C rather than contradictory: uhitm.c:462 splits do_attack() on `is_safemon(mtmp) && !svc.context.forcefight`, and the port's helper covers exactly the arm C reaches when that test fails, which is the ordinary attack arm whether the target is hostile or a pet under the prefix. Renaming it would make the port's name diverge from the C branch it stands for. The comment was separately confirmed as incomplete for a different reason -- it dropped the note that the path is bounded -- and that half was applied. Do not reopen on the name alone without showing the helper covers a branch C does not.

rejections.summary: A finding that the new `import { stop_occupation } from './allmain.js'` closes an allmain to unported_monster_actions cycle and the comment certifies only one direction of it.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator found the cycle pre-existing and harmless under ES modules: the two files already imported from each other before this range, the import is used only inside a closure invoked long after both module bodies have evaluated, and no top-level initialization reads across the cycle. Do not reopen without a load-order case that actually observes a partially initialized binding.

rejections.summary: A finding that the dochugw stopOccupation hook discards occupationEnv.random, so randomness drawn by the finish-meal path it newly enables would come from the live ISAAC stream rather than the clone's.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator traced the finish-meal path and found it draws no randomness: maybe_finished_meal() reaches eatfood() and done_eating(), and every arm the port reaches on that route is deterministic. The concern is real in shape but has no reachable instance today. Do not reopen without naming a call on that path that consumes a random number.

rejections.summary: A finding that the interruption matrix reaches maybe_finished_meal(TRUE) only through moveloop_core(), so the dochugw route -- the only one that runs against the planning clone -- is uncovered for the finished-meal case.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator confirmed the coverage description but rejected the framing: the matrix does cover the dochugw route for the ordinary interruption, and the finished-meal-through-dochugw combination is a narrower gap than the finding claims, already implied by the separately confirmed and deferred dochugw-planning-display-suppression-unpinned entry. Reporting it twice would double-count one gap. Do not reopen separately from that deferral.

deferrals.summary: The dochugw stop_occupation seam in js/unported_monster_actions.js hands stop_occupation() a silent message and a no-op statusRefresh when env.planning is set, and the live ttyPline/bot() pair otherwise, but nothing pins that choice: removing the planning arm and always passing the live pair leaves the full suite green and the four-segment interruption matrix byte-identical, because a planning pass that writes to the live terminal still produces the same recorded screens when the live pass writes the same line afterwards -- the corruption is a duplicate write, not a different one. Deferred rather than applied because a test needs a monster, an installed occupation and a state satisfying assertSimpleActionState(), which is more scaffolding than an audit fix should carry.

mutation.finderConclusion: The range mutation run produced no mutants at all, and the pass was told to treat that as grounds for suspicion rather than comfort. The tests finder confirmed the reading: the range's changed production lines hold almost no relational, logical or boolean sites -- attack_checks()'s force-fight arm is a bare `return false`, the off-edge arm is an assignment and a call, and stop_occupation()'s body is straight-line -- so the empty result carries no evidence either way rather than evidence of coverage. Judging those lines by reading instead found the three gaps the run could not: the printing arm's nomul(0) had no oracle at all, since deleting the statement left the whole suite green while every segment reaching it already has multi 0 and the fields already clear; the planning-mode display suppression was unobservable through the recorded matrix; and the two matrix rows named for an axe never checked that an axe was wielded, so substituting the Valkyrie's long sword for the Barbarian's battle-axe passed. passes.evidence: Counts: 18 raw, 12 deduplicated, 9 confirmed, 9 applied, 0 deferred, 3 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 0 mutants. Full correctness pass over the monsters deferral sweep. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered. No behavioral defect, which is the required result for a behavior-preserving range: the convergence of eleven helpless() spellings onto one definition held at every site when checked against what each previously computed, the moved mon_allowflags() computes what it did before, and the dog_hunger refusals fire before any output or state change. Seven of the nine confirmed findings were wrong C line citations, and that is the result worth keeping. One sat on the single line of production code recording why starvePet refuses rather than being wired, and began seven lines inside a different function. The decisive one was a test citing js/mon.js:972 in the same commit that shifted that code by 95 lines: it was wrong before it was pushed. That settles the argument for a checking script over careful hand-correction, since a citation written correctly can rot inside its own diff, and it is noted on the tracked entry, whose scope now extends past the four files it originally named. Two further comments misdescribed what this range did rather than where it came from: the note justifying the move enumerated the pre-move import while the same commit widened it, and the stopOccupation injection shadows a ported function three lines below a comment saying it is ported. The score is unchanged at 1294 screens and 118144 calls.

productionDefects.summary: js/unported_monster_actions.js cited dogmove.c dog_starve() as (340-358) on the one line of production code that records why starvePet refuses rather than being wired. dog_starve() is dogmove.c:347-358; lines 340-345 are dog_eat()'s tail, ending in `return (DEADMONSTER(mtmp)) ? 2 : 1;`. The comment's substance was right -- dog_starve() does print through You_feel() and call mondied(), neither ported -- but a reader checking it against the cited range sees a different function with a different contract and may conclude the refusal is over-broad and could be wired after all. Corrected to 347-358, and the sibling dog_hunger() citation widened to 360-394 so both span their leading comment and closing brace. Also in the same file, the stopOccupation injection shadows an allmain.c stop_occupation() that is ported and already in the env chain, three lines below a comment telling the reader it is ported; the override is deliberate, because C reaches it at dogmove.c:377 after a You_feel() line that has no owner, so letting the real function through would run the interruption without the announcement preceding it. The comment now says that rather than leaving the contradiction.

rejections.summary: A finding that supplying all three hunger operations as throwing refusals defeats the pre-resolution at js/dogmove.js:373-375, whose purpose is to refuse before the arm runs.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator traced the pre-resolution and found it unaffected: it resolves the operations by name and throws if one is missing, and a supplied operation that itself throws reaches the same named class through the same path. rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator confirmed the unreachability, which is the reason the injection is a refusal rather than a supplier, and rejected the framing: an unreachable arm that fails closed needs no oracle beyond the class it raises, which the three PET_HUNGER_REFUSALS cases already pin.
