passes.evidence: Counts: 23 raw, 22 deduplicated, 19 confirmed, 10 applied, 9 deferred, 3 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 10 survivors of 10 mutants. Full correctness pass over the wish-name-resolution goal, on the largest range this ledger has reviewed: 678 changed production lines in one commit across five files, three of which lay outside the slice's stated boundary and were reached by following a trace. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered. Nineteen confirmed findings, the largest set recorded here. One production defect, and it is this project's most durable pattern: set_artifact_intrinsic() refused after it had already written the hero's extrinsics, the third refusal-after-a-state-change found in five passes. The methodological result is the one worth carrying. The slice's ten mutation survivors were all argued equivalent and all the arguments held, but the pass showed the argument proves less than it looks: the mutator's relational map covers only the four ordering operators, so a strict-inequality line is not an enumerable site and the run is silent about it rather than covering it. A finder demonstrated that by taking such a line, bane_applies()'s SPFX_DALIGN hero arm, and proving with V8 coverage that it never executes. Nine test gaps were found that way, none visible to mutation, and they are deferred as one grouped ledger entry because nine fixtures across four test files exceeds what an audit-fix commit should carry. Two claims that no randomness lay on this path proved false during the work, both on the path the recorded case walks, and the comments asserting them are corrected rather than merely narrowed. The score is unchanged at 1363 screens and 118168 calls across the fixes.

productionDefects.summary: js/artifacts.js set_artifact_intrinsic() wrote the carried-resistance extrinsic into u.uprops through extrinsicMask() and only then read oart.cspfx to refuse the HALRES/ESP/WARN/XRAY group, so the stop fired after the hero extrinsics had already moved. C completes both effects, so C order is correct for C; the port stops on that group, and a refusal that has changed state ends the segment on a screen the port has diverged from rather than on its last matching one. This is the same defect class two earlier passes in this ledger found -- a refusal after rewriting map memory, and a refusal after the object had left inventory -- making it the third instance in five passes and the most durable pattern in this project. Fixed by hoisting the cspfx read and its refusal above the cary lookup and the extrinsicMask() call, leaving the rest of the order as C has it, with a comment stating that this is the one place the port departs from C order and why.

rejections.summary: js/invent.js keeps a private `oname(obj)` that is C's safe_oname(), and this range makes that name collide with a newly exported do_name.js oname() whose contract is entirely different.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: Refuted: this is anchored to an unchanged pre-existing line and duplicates finding [4] from the other side. Counter-evidence: js/invent.js:1419 is not in this range's diff — the invent.js hunks touch only the import block, addinvCore1()/preflightAddinvCores() at 1996-2033, and hold_another_object() at 2643-2672 — so the finding is anchored to code the range did not cause. `node scripts/check-duplicate-symbols.mjs` already grouped this name before the commit: it prints `oname: js/const.js:2878 ONAME (function), js/do_name.js:125 oname (function), js/invent.js:1419 oname (function)`, and the const.js and invent.js members both existed at f748034, so the duplicate index report

rejections.summary: preflightAddinvCores() dropped its `|| obj.oartifact` arm while addinvCore1() gained two new ways to throw for an artifact, so preflight_addinv()'s documented promise that every missing inventory effect is rejected before ownership changes no longer holds — and the mirror-image preflightFreeinvCore(
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The finding reads the doc comment as promising that addinv() cannot throw, but the comment's first sentence scopes it: "Dependency-only half of invent.c addinv_core0()." preflight_addinv()'s job is resolving named injections through requiredHook(), and that coverage is still complete after the change -- addinvCore1()'s new artifact branch (js/invent.js:2001-2008) calls no hook at all, so there is no "missing inventory effect" left unchecked. Its two exits are ported refusals of unported C branches (UnsupportedObjectOperationError / UnsupportedArtifactDisplayError), a different category from an unsupplied hook. Counter-evidence: js/invent.js:2001-2008 contains no requiredHook

rejections.summary: readobjnam_postparse3() now writes d.contents and d.halfeaten, two fields requireSimpleWishQualifiers() validates before the parse loop runs, so the guard's documented invariant ("with the value readobjnam_init() gives each") no longer holds and nothing next to either site says so.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: Half the claim is impossible and the executed evidence for the other half is wrong. The fruit loop's `d.halfeaten = halfeatenf` can only ever write 0: readobjnam_preparse() strips 'partly eaten '/'partially eaten ' first (js/objnam_readobjnam.js:744-746) and sets d.halfeaten, so requireSimpleWishQualifiers() refuses any such wish before postparse3 runs at all. Only d.contents is genuinely written post-guard, and that write is paired with d.typ = TIN in the same two lines. Counter-evidence: `readobjnam('partly eaten slime mold')` refuses with 'a wish that sets halfeaten' -- the field guard, reached before the fruit loop, so halfeatenf is 0 on every path that reaches line 1316

deferrals.summary: The hero branch of bane_applies()'s SPFX_DALIGN arm is never executed by any test.
touch_artifact()'s blast arm for a non-self-willed restricted artifact is never exercised: every hero test stubs rn2 to a nonzero value, so `!rn2(4)` is always false.
The bare assert.throws for the Orb of Detection accepts a refusal that has already written an extrinsic into u.uprops, and does not check that the state is untouched.
The confers_luck assertion that claims to cover SPFX_LUCK uses an artifact that has no SPFX_LUCK, and passes only through the LUCKSTONE short-circuit above it.
The oname() truncation test uses only ASCII, so the byte-versus-code-point semantics its comment calls out are not pinned by any assertion.
addinv_core1()'s quest-artifact refusal has no test, and unlike the four sibling special-object arms it is absent from preflightAddinvCores().
The test titled "each arm of the postparse3 tail" skips the fruit block entirely; the two mutation survivors inside it are zero coverage, not the equivalence the slice claimed.
The test named for the d->dn and d->origbp lookups has no oracle that either lookup ran: both can be deleted outright and the whole suite stays green.
The only test guarding the ARMOR_CLASS retry against an infinite loop kills a wrong implementation by hanging the test runner, not by failing.

passes.evidence: Counts: 19 raw, 17 deduplicated, 9 confirmed, 8 applied, 1 deferred, 8 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 1 survivors of 1 mutants. Full correctness pass over the movement-while-riding goal. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered. No behavioral defect, but nine confirmed findings of which three were claims that would mislead the next reader into breaking something, and two of those this loop had repeated in its own records. The sharpest: deleting domove()'s riding refusal left trapmove()'s mounted-hero stop still documented as the second lock on the same door, when it is now the only one, so acting on the sentence would make a mounted hero in a bear trap print the unmounted lines where C names the steed. The pass also judged the slice's own remedy inadequate, which is what it was asked to do: the slice had found that opening a segment with a wait moves mount_steed()'s impairment roll so the hero slips and every later key walks on foot while the differential still passes, and added two assertions that test a string segmentFor() composes rather than the case table, so neither could catch what they were written for. Two justifications were wrong about C, one of them this loop's own reason for trusting the forecast: movemon() does not skip u.usteed, and monmove.c:966's mpeaceful gate is what keeps a tame steed out of mattacku(). One finding is deferred: js/mhitu.js is executed by no fresh segment, so a file that exists because of a random-number call has no recorded C evidence, and a wrong draw there shifts the PRNG log rather than a screen. The score is unchanged at 1373 screens and 118557 calls across the fixes.

rejections.summary: The failed-pet-swap restore is unreachable dead code that the running game never executes, and the comment justifying it states a premise about C that is false for one of the six FALSE arms.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The headline correctness claim does not survive. The block is a byte-faithful translation of hack.c:2922-2926 (`u.ux = u.ux0, u.uy = u.uy0;` then the guarded steed write), guarded by the callee's own return value, so it cannot execute wrongly and cannot execute at all today. Nothing in it is incorrect. Counter-evidence: AGENTS.md's first implementation rule requires translating whole C functions and matching "the C code's branches", which is what an `if (!domove_swap_with_pet(...))` arm around an already-live call is; the 'do not prepare code for future branches' rule targets

rejections.summary: The failed-pet-swap restore added at domove_core():2921-2926 has no test, no reachable caller, and no mutation site, so nothing in the repository distinguishes it from a wrong restore.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The facts are right but do not constitute a test defect. passes.evidence: Counts: 9 raw, 8 deduplicated, 6 confirmed, 6 applied, 0 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 805 survivors of 879 mutants. Full correctness pass over the options-simple-menu goal. Four mandatory finders; neither optional finder was triggered. Two production findings sharing one root cause, and together the most consequential this ledger holds: the range retired a display refusal on the claim that this port keeps no glyph-to-symbol-and-color table, and loc.remembered_glyph is exactly that table. The pass proved it by execution -- turning color on from the O menu leaves a remembered out-of-sight door at NO_COLOR where C repaints it CLR_BROWN -- so a clean fail-closed stop had become a silent wrong screen on a row the menu lists. hilite_pile is the worse half, because this port records no piletop mark at all and cannot re-highlight a remembered pile even in principle. Restoring the refusal costs the goal every development screen it had earned, since seed0006 picks hilite_pile at step 64, and that is the right trade: a stopped segment is worth more than one that runs on painting wrong cells. The underlying representation gap -- map memory storing a resolved presentation where C stores an unresolved glyph number -- is recorded as the new ledger entry remembered-glyph-caches-a-resolved-presentation, which is a display-subsystem goal rather than a finding of this range. The pass earned its place twice over on method. The goal's own trace had been wrong about the same function, so every claim from it was re-checked rather than carried, which is what surfaced the defect. And the mutation numbers said it first: 805 survivors sound alarming and 803 are boolean flips in a generated table pinned byte for byte by check:options, but of the two in hand-written code, one the slice never reported was the tell -- after the retirement opt_need_glyph_reset was written in four places and read nowhere. One finding was tried and reverted rather than applied, and the comment records why: the offered fix for give_opt_msg's three-valued read seeds a field in the parse result rather than the game state, so it never reaches the read and silences four toggle messages. The score ends where the goal began, at 1373 screens.

productionDefects.summary: The range retired js/options.js reset_needed_visuals()'s reset_glyphmap(gm_optionchange) refusal on the claim that this port keeps no glyph-to-symbol-and-color table, so a docrt() repaint would answer the whole question. The claim is false and the pass proved it by execution rather than argument. loc.remembered_glyph IS that table: remembered_glyph_from_presentation() stores an already-resolved {ch, color, decgfx, attr}, with the colour already pushed through mapColorEnabled(), and newsym()'s out-of-sight arm replays those fields without recomputing any of them. Measured: with OPTIONS=!color, walking until a door is remembered and out of sight and then picking the color row from the O menu, in-sight cells recolour correctly while the door stays NO_COLOR where C repaints it CLR_BROWN. hilite_pile is the worse half, and is a second confirmed finding with the same root: C carries piletop-ness as MG_OBJPILE in glyphmap[] and applies ATR_INVERSE at every print, while this port bakes the attribute in at draw time and records no piletop mark at all, so a remembered pile cannot be re-highlighted even in principle. That converted a clean fail-closed stop into a silent wrong screen on a row the O menu lists and the range's own recipe picks. Fixed by restoring the refusal, which costs seed0006 the five screens the pick loop earned because it picks hilite_pile at step 64; the development score returns from 1378 to 1373. The test asserting the repaint was inverted rather than deleted so the refusal has an oracle. The mutation survivor at js/options.js:4120 was the tell: after the retirement opt_need_glyph_reset was written in four places and read nowhere.

The same retirement loses hilite_pile, and this half cannot be recovered later even in principle. C carries piletop-ness as the MG_OBJPILE bit that reset_glyphmap() stores in glyphmap[], and wintty.c applies ATR_INVERSE from that bit at every print, so a repaint re-highlights remembered piles. This port bakes ATR_INVERSE into remembered_glyph.attr at draw time from the live iflags.hilite_pile (js/display.js:1136-1142) and records no piletop mark at all, so after the toggle a remembered pile is redrawn with the attribute it had before, and nothing in map memory says it was ever a pile. hilite_pile is a row on the recorded first page of the simple menu and the range own recipe picks it deliberately, so any game where the hero walked past a pile before opening O showed the pile un-highlighted where C shows it inverse. Closed by the same restored refusal.

Full four-finder audit-diff-correctness pass over the pray-command goal, verified adversarially in three batches. 24 raw findings, 23 after deduplication, 19 confirmed, 4 rejected, none left unverified; all 19 applied in 34516de. The development score is identical either side of the fixes at 1388/7765 screens and 118743/610816 calls, measured by me at b0bb30e and again at 34516de. Two confirmed findings were behavioral and both were invariants that went stale rather than code that was wrong when written: pray.c critically_low_hp() had been ported a second time while the first copy kept serving botl.c and wintty.c with C's Upolyd arm missing, and dopray()'s nomul(-3) became the port's first negative-multi call site, falsifying the reason js/uhitm.js hitum() gave for dropping C's gm.multi < 0 term. The first was converged onto one owner; the second was re-derived from uhitm.c, which reads that term after passive() and so answers only for a paralysis inflicted inside the blow, leaving the port correct for a different reason than the one it stated.

productionDefects.summary: pray.c critically_low_hp() was ported twice and the two copies disagreed. The goal added a canonical js/pray.js critically_low_hp() while the pre-existing private js/display.js _criticallyLowHp() stayed in place, and that copy omitted C's Upolyd arm, so a polymorphed hero read u.uhp/u.uhpmax where C reads u.mh/u.mhmax. The display copy is not dormant: it serves botl.c:2555, which asks critically_low_hp(FALSE) for the BL_HP field, and win/tty/wintty.c:4539, which asks critically_low_hp(TRUE) for the hit-point bar, so the status line and the prayer could answer differently about the same hero. AGENTS.md's Keep each game value in one place governs. Fixed by deleting _criticallyLowHp() and pointing both C sites at js/pray.js critically_low_hp() with the argument each C site passes; verified that botl.c passes FALSE and wintty.c passes TRUE. The development score is unchanged because no recorded session polymorphs, which is exactly why the divergence survived until a second port of the same function exposed it. check:duplicate-symbols fell from 287 to 285.

The same defect reported independently by the variable-trace finder, which reached it from the other end: the range added a second port of one C function without deleting or repointing the first, so the port held two answers for one C value. Two finders converging on one duplicate from opposite directions is why it was treated as a defect rather than as tidying.

Porting do_wear.c stuck_ring() left js/insight.js:539-541 refusing insight.c one_characteristic()'s Fixed_abil arm with the reason stuck_ring() ... not ported, which the same range had made false. A refusal whose stated reason no longer holds is a fail-open in waiting: it stops a path that is now portable, and the next reader has no way to tell whether the stop is still needed. Fixed by porting the arm from C and removing the refusal.

The new restricted arm of tty_yn_function() added a module-private QUITCHARS as a second copy of decl.c quitchars[], while js/const.js:2014 already exported quitchars with the same value and the same C citation. Fixed by deleting the private copy and importing the existing one.

It sustained all nine: js/cmd.js:451 and :456 sit in paranoid_ynq()'s accept_q arm, which paranoid_query() never enables; js/pray.js:183 is maxhp > hplim, where the >= mutant reassigns an already-equal value; js/pray.js:303 is i < A_MAX, where the <= mutant reads one past the array and compares undefined; and js/pray.js:606, 609, 613, 614 and 645 clamp or assign at boundaries where the mutated comparison writes the value already there. readiness.sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable before the ending events was traced against nethack-c/upstream/: pray.c dopray() (2199-2273), can_pray() (2124-2172), in_trouble() (198-288), worst_cursed_item() (288-373), critically_low_hp() (116-156), stuck_in_wall() (161-181), blocked_boulder(), prayer_done() (2276-2343) head and p_type 0 arm, gods_upset() (1435-1445) and angrygods() (703-784); hack.c unmul() (4176-4208); allmain.c moveloop_core() (379-388); eat.c gethungry() (3174); trap.c unconscious() (6775-6786); region.c region_danger(); do_wear.c stuck_ring() and unchanger(); cmd.c doextcmd(), paranoid_ynq() and paranoid_query(); and win/tty/topl.c tty_yn_function() and update_topl() (262). The trace covered state, random-number order and the points where the game waits for input. It found no behavioral divergence inside the boundary, and four C citations in the changed blocks that read low: dopray() cited as ending at 2276 when it ends at 2273, gethungry() cited at 3173 when the test is at 3174, and angrygods() and gods_upset() bracketed to include a leading comment or the next function's signature. passes.evidence: Counts: 23 raw, 21 deduplicated, 16 confirmed, 16 applied, 0 deferred, 5 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 3 survivors of 11 mutants. Full four-finder audit-diff-correctness pass over objects-deferral-sweep-2, verified adversarially. 23 raw findings, 21 after deduplication, 16 confirmed, 5 rejected, none left unverified; all 16 applied in f6a3350. The development score is identical either side of the fixes at 1389/7765 screens and 118859/610816 calls, measured by me at 1792cdc and again at f6a3350, and identical session for session. One confirmed finding was behavioral: makewish() handed an async hook to hold_another_object(), which invokes it through the synchronous merged() and drops the promise, so the merge message was neither ordered before obfree() nor awaited before the inventory line. No development session merges a wish into a carried stack, so the score could never have shown it. The rest were nine falsified or misstated comments and six test gaps where the code under test could be deleted with the whole suite green. The readiness mutation left three survivors in one function and the pass resolved them as an artifact of a narrower wave, then found the real issue beside them: a range simplification whose validity depends on an object-table adjacency that nothing pinned.

productionDefects.summary: js/zap.js makewish() supplied an async inventoryComparisonDiscovered hook to hold_another_object(), which invokes it through the synchronous merged() and discards the returned promise. The message invent.c merged() (933-942) prints when a wished object merges into a carried stack -- "You learn more about your items by comparing them." -- was therefore neither ordered before obfree() nor awaited before the inventory line. The hook had been added a few commits earlier because a scan found it missing, so the path is live rather than hypothetical. Fixed by awaiting addinvCore0Runtime() in hold_another_object(). It is invisible to the development score because no development session merges a wish into a carried stack, which is exactly why the pass was worth running: the defect sits on a live path the recorded set does not traverse. The apply session then built the end-to-end guard the pass had judged possibly expensive -- a Rogue wishing for an uncursed +0 dagger merges into the starting stack on all five seeds tried, and naming uncursed +0 removes the BUC and enchantment rolls that would otherwise make the merge seed-dependent. That test fails against the pre-fix ordering, so one guard now covers both this defect and the coverage gap reported beside it.

readiness.boundary: A deferred-area sweep has no single user-visible boundary; each slice carries its ledger entry as its own. The four that changed reachable behavior: pressing i with a hero wearing gloves, from the keystroke to the inventory menu C paints; submitting a container at the wizard wish prompt, from the newline to the inventory line and the contents mkbox_cnts() places; pressing T on a suit with a non-zero delay, from the keystroke through five helpless turns to the finish message; and escaping an empty wish line, from the Escape to the object mkobj() builds reaching hold_another_object(). The real game executes all four, and fresh C recordings match: run-worn-glove-name.mjs 6 segments and 18196 calls, run-wished-container.mjs 13 and 34419, run-take-off-armor.mjs 17 and 51255, run-random-wish.mjs 21 and 56981.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable before those endings was traced against nethack-c/upstream/: objnam.c doname_base() (1387-1417), readobjnam() with its any arm (4994-4996), typfnd tail (5037) and spe switch (5122-5165), and readobjnam_postparse3() (4726-4899); do_wear.c armoroff() (1930-1972), Armor_off() (908-930), donning() (1571-1596) and doffing() (1601-1640); mkobj.c mksobj() (1010-1021), mkbox_cnts() (303-384) and the probability walk in mkobj() (270-301); invent.c addinv_core0 and core1 (960-1085) and merged() (933-942); eat.c set_tin_variety(); and obj.h is_poisonable() (264-268) and Is_dragon_armor() (346-352). The trace covered state, random-number order and the points where the game waits for input. It found one behavioral divergence, an async hook invoked synchronously, and nine comments the range had falsified or misstated, including two files that each claimed to be the sole writer of state.afternmv, a claim that was true of one of them until this range added the second.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the four boundaries. Every reachable excluded branch stops before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output. The one omission that looked like a fail-open was checked rather than assumed: C entire globby branch is omitted on the new mkobj() arm, and the walk at mkobj.c 290-292 subtracts each row oc_prob from a prob that starts at 1 or more, so a row whose oc_prob is 0 can never be the stopping row; all four GLOB_OF rows carry 0, and a test now fails if one is given a non-zero probability. Excluded and verified fail-closed: CHEST, LARGE_BOX and ICE_BOX on the wish path; ARM_HELM, ARM_GLOVES and ARM_BOOTS in armoroff(); uskin in the worn-armor naming arm; and named wishes for tin, egg, slime mold, statue, figurine and corpse. Four gaps are recorded rather than closed: the three box types, helms and gloves and boots, the unrestricted prompt arm, and wish-name-that-matches-nothing blocked on wizterrainwish.

passes.evidence: Counts: 6 raw, 5 deduplicated, 4 confirmed, 4 applied, 0 deferred, 0 rejected, 1 unverified; mutation: 1 survivors of 10 mutants. Full four-finder pass over the monster-drops-equipped-gear boundary port, one commit changing 71 lines of one file. 6 raw findings, 5 after deduplication, 4 confirmed and all 4 applied, none rejected, and one left unverified when its adjudicator died. I judged that one myself and applied it too, so eccdb8b carries five fixes; counts.applied records only the confirmed set, as the schema requires. The development score is identical either side at 1410/7765 screens and 119046/610816 calls. No production behaviour changed: three findings were false statements about what gates the port's unported arms, one was a missing test for a C-to-JS translation seam, and the unverified one was that seam's comment claiming a faithful translation when C's strchr on a NUL byte and the port's includes(0) disagree at exactly one input. The apply session corrected the pass itself on the sharpest finding: the endArtifactLight hook is held unreachable by a nearer and wider refusal than the pass identified, because mdrop_obj() names the object through distant_name() before extracting it, so the recommended extra refusal would have been unreachable code.

mutation.deltaRun: The audit-fix diff at eccdb8b produced no mutants: its js/ change is comment text only, and the two new assertions are tests. Its trailer sits in the same final paragraph as Assisted-by:, so git reads it.
mutation.finderConclusion: The readiness run left exactly one survivor, js/steal.js:265:43, the silently argument, which the slice worker had predicted and argued unkillable. It holds: silently is read only by extract_from_minvent() update_mon_extrinsics() call, which do_extrinsics false makes unreachable by C own argument at steal.c 841-843, every caller of mdrop_obj() passes the same false, and scripts/worn.test.mjs:330-353 covers both values directly. The more useful observation is what the mutation run could not see at all: three of the four confirmed findings are false statements in comments, and the fourth is a missing test for a translation seam. No mutation kind reaches any of those, which is why a range this small still repaid a full four-finder pass.

The trace covered state, random-number order and the points where the game waits for input. It found no behavioural divergence and four false or incomplete statements about what gates the unported arms, three of which this range wrote. The pass itself was wrong on one of them and the apply session corrected it against C: the endArtifactLight hook is held unreachable not by makemon_create m_dowear_type() missing begin_burn, as the pass argued from a trace that called extract_from_minvent() directly, but by js/objnam.js preflightDoname() refusing any lamplit worn object inside distant_name(), which mdrop_obj() calls first and which is strictly wider than the arm test.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behaviour remains inside the boundary. The one deliberate departure from the usual ordering is that the tail refusal now fires after the object has been extracted and placed, because C puts update_mon_extrinsics() after the drop for its own stated reason; the pass confirmed that ordering against steal.c 841-845. Excluded and verified fail-closed: update_mon_extrinsics() behind the DEADMONSTER guard, and mwepgone() supplied as a named refusal so a widened wield boundary ends a segment rather than throwing an untyped Error. The endArtifactLight arm is unreachable through a proper boundary rather than a bare Error, now pinned by a test that fails with the crash if the near gate is removed. Two gaps stay recorded rather than closed: mwepgone-has-no-reachable-consumer, and the saddle exemption, which ships unreachable in the running game with unit cover and a comment naming what would exercise it. roomno cannot be 0 at the in_rooms test: costly_spot() answers only through inside_shop(), which returns NO_ROOM for any roomno below ROOMOFFSET, so C strchr on a NUL and the port includes(0) cannot disagree there.

passes.evidence: Counts: 17 raw, 16 deduplicated, 13 confirmed, 12 applied, 1 deferred, 3 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 1 survivors of 9 mutants. Full four-finder pass over the zap-command goal, the port's first zap of any kind. 17 raw findings, 16 after deduplication, 13 confirmed, 3 rejected, none unverified; 12 applied in 1435470 and 1 deferred. The development score is identical either side at 1431/7765 screens and 120151/610816 calls, because nothing behavioural changed. Seven confirmed findings were comments that were false, self-contradicting or cited the wrong C statements, and five were untested lines whose deletion left the whole suite green. The sharpest was one this range caused: hack.c overexert_hp()'s refusal was justified by a comment saying none of its three statements was ported, and this range ported fall_asleep(). It stays refused, and the apply session found the gate the pass itself had missed -- js/allmain.js refuses a hero immobile and burdened at once, which the fainting arm produces by construction, so porting it would relocate the stop inside one round rather than win a screen, while spending a new draw and changing what overexertion() returns to a caller in uhitm.c. The deferred finding is a live divergence this range made reachable: ambient lines skip C's Unaware wording for a sleeping hero, with no observed instance in any development session.

productionDefects.summary: js/sounds.js paints ambient lines with a hard-coded "You hear " prefix instead of routing through pline.c You_hear(), so it skips that function Unaware branch: C paints "You dream that you hear ..." for a hero who is asleep or fainted, at pline.c 446-447. js/mon.js carries the same defect. This range made the branch reachable for the first time, because timeout.c fall_asleep() sets u.usleep, so unconscious() answers true and Unaware holds for the roughly 27 turns a self-zap of sleep costs; C own commented-out block at timeout.c 959-960 names the coupling. It costs nothing measurable today, and that was checked rather than assumed: no development session records a "dream that you hear" line across all 33 session files, and seed0016, the one session that sleeps, records no ambient line during the sleep. Deferred rather than applied because js/sounds.js is outside the reviewed range, the fix ports two new You_hear() branches and changes what is rendered, and AGENTS.md wants a fresh C recording before that counts as complete.

passes.evidence: Counts: 22 raw, 20 deduplicated, 16 confirmed, 16 applied, 0 deferred, 4 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 40 mutants. Two production defects and one wrong refusal were introduced by this goal and fixed in its audit-fix commit 52c6513. The one that mattered is same_remembered_glyph(): the goal's own slice-selector had flagged the coarseness as a known residual and the code comment said so, but nobody had asked whether it was observable. It is, on the single path the goal made live, where it decides whether applying a lock pick costs a turn. Two finders reached it independently from different directions. The development score is identical before and after the audit fix at 1458/7765 screens, 120419/610816 calls, 1484/7765 cursors and 7 of 33 sessions, so none of the sixteen findings changed a recorded path; the goal's whole +27 screens came from the two implementation commits. Applying the sixteen took a further 2521 seconds beyond the pass's own 3221.

productionDefects.summary: same_remembered_glyph() answered "unchanged" for two remembered corpses C calls changed, because it compared a drawn presentation where C compares a glyph number. display.h corpse_to_glyph() encodes corpsenm, so a jackal corpse and a sewer-rat corpse carry different numbers while sharing symbol and colour; the finder executed both against the worktree and got byte-identical records. lock.c:584 is the sole consumer, and its result reaches doapply() at apply.c:4288 as the ECMD_TIME choice, so a wrong answer costs or saves a whole turn of monster movement and random-number draws. Fixed by stamping objectGlyphId in object_glyph_info(), carrying otyp, oclass, corpsenm and statue gender with a pile-top suffix, copying it as a non-enumerable sidecar in remembered_glyph_from_presentation(), and adding it to REMEMBERED_GLYPH_IDENTITY_FIELDS. The end-to-end C recording needs a pile top to change while the hero cannot see the square, which could not be arranged; that gap is recorded as pick-lock-lookalike-pile-top-has-no-fresh-case.

The same same_remembered_glyph() defect reached independently from the object side: two floor objects of different otyp that draw with one class symbol and colour compared equal, where C compares objnum_to_glyph(otyp) values that differ. The finder proved it by probe, mapping an otyp 2 object, blinding the hero, replacing it with otyp 21 of the same class and colour, and applying a lock pick: the remembered record was byte-identical and doapply() returned ECMD_OK where C returns ECMD_TIME. One adjudicator refuted this on causality as a duplicate of the corpse finding while the mandatory source-trace lens confirmed it, so it stands as its own record of a second reachable case. Fixed by the same objectGlyphId change, and pinned separately by an ARROW versus CROSSBOW_BOLT test.

reglyph_darkroom() refused more than its justification supported. Only two of C's four arms at display.c:1826-1848 need GLYPH_NOTHING; the two behind dark_room and colour need only the cmap index this same range added, so a remembered lit corridor kept S_litcorr where C rewrites it to S_corr, and an O-menu lit_corridor toggle repainted out-of-sight corridor cells in CLR_WHITE where C paints the terminal default. Fixed by running display.c:1831-1833 and 1842-1844 inside the non-refused branch, keeping the refusal for the two GLYPH_NOTHING arms, and adding C's third gate term Is_rogue_level(), which the port had ignored.

The pet cursed-step report hallucinated only the pile name. do_name.c noit_mon_nam() passes SUPPRESS_SADDLE|SUPPRESS_IT without SUPPRESS_HALLUCINATION, so x_monnam()'s do_hallu arm replaces the pet's name with rndmonnam() and draws twice from the display RNG; the port printed the true species name, drew nothing, and the committed test pinned that wrong string. Fixed by raising UnsupportedMonsterNameError from alwaysVisibleMonsterName() under Hallucination, which fails closed before any message or draw and also covers hack.c domove_swap_with_pet() at 2170, whose C line omits the same flag. The port rather than the refusal was rejected because peffect_hallucination() is unported, so the path is unreachable today.

Counter-evidence: js/display.js:1428-1432 does not attribute glyph-number content to the accessibility sidecars: it says "the first is what C's glyph number carries for a piece of terrain, the other two describe hero-memory mimics and hiders". mutation.deltaRun: The audit-fix diff at 52c6513 mutated 10 and killed 10. Its first run left two survivors, the new reglyph_darkroom() loop’s x < COLNO and y < ROWNO bounds, unkillable because a null-location guard made the extra iteration a no-op; deleting that guard killed both. The guard was dead code in the new loop rather than an existing one: makeCoordinateGrid() in js/game.js fills every cell of the COLNO x ROWNO grid with a truthy makeLocation(), so at() answers non-null for every in-bounds coordinate, which the orchestrator verified rather than accepted.
mutation.finderConclusion: The readiness run over the frozen range mutated 31 and killed 31 before the pass ran, the first range in this loop to enter a correctness pass with no survivors; re-run over the recorded range including the audit fixes, it mutated 40 and killed 40. readiness.boundary: Two user-visible paths. First, a pet stepping onto a square holding a cursed object, from the pet move through the report line to the screen it paints; seed1500-rogue-explore-move executes it and the port matches C on it, and four fresh C recordings cover it directly. Second, applying a lock pick, credit card or skeleton key and answering the direction prompt with a square that holds no door, from the keystroke through the prompt to the message and the turn the command costs or does not cost; five fresh C recordings cover it over 15 segments. The real game executes both: seed1500 now matches 40 of 40 screens, 2768 of 2768 random-number calls and 40 of 40 cursors, the seventh of 33 development sessions to match completely.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable before those endings was traced against nethack-c/upstream/: lock.c pick_lock() 578-593; dogmove.c dog_move() 1298-1312; pline.c pline_mon() 138-150; dungeon.c update_mapseen_for() 2941-2947, update_lastseentyp() and recalc_mapseen(); display.c feel_location() 859-901 with the _map_location macro 448-472 and the dark-room tail 893-900, reglyph_darkroom() 1826-1848 and its call site at options.c initoptions_finish():7347; engrave.c engr_can_be_felt() 291-313; apply.c doapply() 4288; do_name.c noit_Monnam() and noit_mon_nam() 1054-1089 and x_monnam()’s do_hallu arm; defsym.h:113. The trace covered state, random-number order and the points where the game waits for input. It found three C citations in the changed code wrong and corrected them: recalc_mapseen() closes at dungeon.c:3261 rather than 3278 and update_lastseentyp() sits at 3192 rather than 3191; display.c:1845-1847 is in the else arm rather than behind the option gate; and feel_location()’s new header stated a caller contract false for js/hack.js:1718, which passes a DOOR square.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside either boundary. Excluded and verified fail-closed: feel_location()’s Underwater, Levitation and Punished bc_felt states behind one guard; its sensed-monster tail, whose UnsupportedMapMemoryError is hoisted above every map-memory write so the stop leaves the map untouched; reglyph_darkroom()’s two GLYPH_NOTHING arms and the rogue level; pick_lock()’s monster and door-mimic arms at 560-577, its container branch, its interrupted-attempt resume and the doormask default arm; and alwaysVisibleMonsterName() under Hallucination. Three gaps are recorded rather than closed: pick-lock-drawbridge-message-has-no-fresh-case, because create_drawbridge() is reached only from Castle and Medusa description files no ported level generates; pick-lock-lookalike-pile-top-has-no-fresh-case, because the pile top must change while the hero cannot see the square; and feel-location-ported-twice, the duplicate partial port in js/detect.js, which carries a reachable lit_corridor divergence and a corrected note replacing the pass’s "strict subset" claim.

passes.evidence: Counts: 18 raw, 16 deduplicated, 11 confirmed, 11 applied, 0 deferred, 5 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 162 survivors of 367 mutants. Counts: 18 raw, 16 deduplicated, 11 confirmed, 11 applied, 0 deferred, 5 rejected, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. Full pass, five finders: correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace and the concurrency finder, enabled because the range made enlightenment() async and introduced the cmd.c command queue as shared mutable state. Range mutation at head: 367 mutants, 205 killed, 162 survived, a 55.9 per cent first-wave kill rate; survivors concentrated in js/dothrow.js (94), js/eat.js (21) and js/cmd.js (17), most of them first-wave artefacts because a test file reaching a module only through another js/ module is excluded from the first wave. One production defect: js/zap.js:599 inverted zap.c:3930 rn2(3), so a thrown missile stuck to a web on two draws in three where C sticks it on one. scripts/bhit.test.mjs asserted the inverted condition, so the oracle certified the defect instead of catching it -- a test pinned to the code rather than to the C source. The corrected test was observed failing against the old line before the fix landed. The rest were structural: rhack() gated the command-queue pop on firstTime where cmd.c:3642 pops unconditionally; five boolean-wrapper arms bypassed the new clear_kickedloc(); two comments asserted guarantees the code no longer provided; and four test oracles proved less than they claimed, including a tautological assert.ok(before - afterFirst <= before). The development score is identical before and after the audit fix at 9/33 sessions, 1512/7765 screens, 120847/610816 calls and 1531/7765 cursors, so none of the eleven findings changed a recorded path; the web arm is unreachable in every development session, which is why the defect survived to a formal pass. Audit-fix mutation: 7 mutants, 7 killed, 0 survived. Note that mutate-sites does not rewrite === into !==, so the exact defect has no mutant of its own and no mutation run could have found it; the integer mutants on that operand cover the branch but not the inversion. Two ledger entries added: a note on eat-corpse-arms-without-a-fresh-case recording that every S_PUDDING row carries G_NOCORPSE (monsters.h:2081-2114), so no C recording can reach the pudding arm, and bhit-web-arm-without-a-fresh-case, because the corrected web arm still has no fresh C differential.

productionDefects.summary: js/zap.js:599 inverted zap.c:3930. C sticks a thrown missile to a web on `!rn2(3)`, one draw in three; the port entered the arm when rn2(3) was non-zero, two in three. The arm consumes randomness and prints a line, so any session that threw into a web would desynchronise the PRNG stream from that point. It reached a formal pass because no development session throws into a web, and because scripts/bhit.test.mjs asserted the inverted condition: the oracle was pinned to the code rather than to the C source, so breaking the line did fail the test and the test still certified the defect. Fixed to `random.rn2(3) === 0`, matching the `allow_skip = random.rn2(3) === 0` spelling ten lines earlier in the same function. The corrected test was observed failing against the old line first, and now covers all three draws rather than two. No mutation run could have found this: mutate-sites does not rewrite === into !==, so the inversion has no mutant of its own.

readiness.boundary: The starting and ending events are user-visible and the real game executes each path: every ported unit was proven by a recorded development session advancing through it, not by a unit test. seed0107 reaches 98 of 98 screens, seed1150 51 of 51 and seed0200 39 of 40, each measured by the orchestrator with npm run checkpoint at the merge commit rather than taken from a worker report.
readiness.sourceReview: Each slice worker traced its own C against nethack-c/upstream/ and reported branch, state and PRNG order. The orchestrator verified every slice outcome independently and checked specific claims at source (display.c 1077-1097, wintty.c 2728-2733, insight.c 1334-1463, frozen/terminal.js 679-685, zap.c 3928-3930, mutate-sites formatTrailer). The orchestrator did not personally re-trace all 4,249 changed lines, which is why the pass was run. Three worker claims were found wrong and corrected during the session: that feel_location() holds a demotion identical to newsym()s, that invent.c display_pickinv() owns the menu clip, and a transposed Mutants trailer. The applying agent refuted four further finding details at source, including a claim that #wizintrinsic calls enlightenment(MAGICENLIGHTENMENT).

Two gaps are recorded rather than closed: the corrected bhit web arm has no fresh C differential (bhit-web-arm-without-a-fresh-case), and eatcorpse()s pudding arm cannot be reached by any C recording because every S_PUDDING row carries G_NOCORPSE (monsters.h:2081-2114). A pre-existing fold in the five boolean-wrapper arms remains: for an elapsed command C runs no reset_cmd_vars() at all, while those arms run one and restore context.move. It is unreachable until make_blinded() or a blindfold is ported and is recorded in the comment at js/cmd.js:2277-2285.

checklist.reason: The goal changed 102 production lines in one area across three slices in a single agent session, under every AGENTS.md threshold that requires a checklist; the existing checklist stopped at 9e68fa6, before this range.

passes.evidence: Counts: 13 raw, 13 deduplicated, 8 confirmed, 8 applied, 0 deferred, 5 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 7 mutants. Full pass, four finders: correctness, readability, tests and variable-trace. The performance and concurrency finders were not enabled and no finder disputed that: the range adds two guard conjuncts, a message selection and a recorded case, with no shared mutable state and no asynchronous or lifecycle change. The pass confirmed no production defect, which is the result that matters here -- the two ported guards and the platform arm survived four perspectives and a clean 7-of-7 mutation run. Six of the eight confirmed findings were assertions that could not fail, and the one that mattered most was the liquid-sound test's single trailing assert.deepEqual(draws(), []): arena() calls initRng() and clears the log, so that assertion inspected only the last of eight cases and the comment justifying it stated a false premise, that IS_SOFT() covers both liquids. rm.h:76 puts LAVAPOOL at 20, outside IS_POOL's 16 to 19, so a lava landing does reach breaktest() and does spend obj_resists()'s rn2(100). The port was right and the test was blind: every case now asserts its own draws, and the two lava cases assert the draw C takes. The development score is identical before and after the audit fix at 9/33 sessions, 1513/7765 screens, 120847/610816 calls and 1531/7765 cursors, so none of the eight findings changed a recorded path; the range's own single screen was seed0016 step 7, delivered by the fprefx() commit before this pass ran.

rejections.summary: js/dothrow.js:144 propertyHeld()'s doc comment enumerates four properties and two call sites while the same commit adds a fifth property, DEAF, and a third call site through Deaf().
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: the comment does not state the contract the finding attributes to it. js/dothrow.js:144-148 enumerates the four youprop.h macros propertyHeld stands in for, and the two gates it names are exactly the callers of those four: :425 reads STONE_RES for the bare-handed corpse gate and :450-451 and :458 read CONFUSION, STUNNED and FUMBLING for the multishot gate. DEAF is never claimed to be one of the four; its complete C union, including the u.uroleplay.deaf term, is spelled in Deaf()'s own comment at :154-157. Do not reopen without a reading of :144-148 that shows it claiming to enumerate every caller of propertyHeld rather than the four macros it replaces.

rejections.summary: js/dothrow.js:158 Deaf()'s comment names js/display.js as the one other place spelling C's Deaf union, while six other modules carry their own copy under four names.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: the comment names js/display.js as a place that spells the same union, not as the only one. js/dothrow.js:154-157 reads 'js/display.js statusConditionActive() spells the same union for the status line' -- an example, with no 'only' and no 'the other'. The finding's own inventory is also incomplete: grep for uroleplay across js/ additionally returns js/apply.js:80 heroDeaf() and js/dogmove.js:220 heroDeaf(), so the union is spelled in nine other modules rather than the six it lists. Do not reopen without a quotation from the comment asserting exclusivity.

rejections.summary: The port models two different C build configurations with no single statement of which it targets: js/eat.js takes the MACOS arm while js/tty_startup.js:27 hard-codes a Unix version banner.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: the port models one build and records it in two places. js/eat.js:1727-1736, added by this range, states the build from primary sources: build-recorder.sh:31-35, config.h:18, config1.h:43-45 and the MACOS9/__BEOS__ guard at :64-67. The QUALITY.json apple entry carries the same analysis and explicitly demotes the banner -- 'The startup banner is corroboration but not proof, and this entry does not rest on it.' The banner in js/tty_startup.js:22-28 is one fixed recorded-startup string, and frozen/ps_test_runner.mjs:68-80 collapses any Version line before comparing, so it models nothing. Do not reopen without evidence that the two files imply different values for a macro the port branches on.

rejections.summary: scripts/run-twoweapon-command.mjs:556 verifyInventory() destructures stack with no default while every sibling field has one, so a case omitting it fails with a message naming the same slot on both sides of the comparison.
rejections.counterEvidence: causality refute: the mechanics are real -- an omitted field gives null !== undefined and both operands render through ?? 'neither' -- but the impact is not material. All six INVENTORY_CASES entries at :183-211 spell stack explicitly, and three spell it as stack: null for exactly the no-stack situation the finding says a maintainer would express by omission, so the file's own convention already answers the hypothesised mistake and the contradictory string cannot fire for any existing case or for one written by copying an existing one. resolution refute: the proposed validation cannot distinguish fixed from faulty, because verifyInventory() is reached only through runTwoWeaponCommandMatrix() and adding a seventh case fails first on the six-role list at scripts/twoweapon-matrix.test.mjs:141-149, so the observed failure would be the role list rather than the predicted message. Do not reopen without a case that reaches the message, which needs a fresh C recording of a temporary recipe.

rejections.summary: scripts/twoweapon-matrix.test.mjs:164's segment-uniqueness assertion compares whole serialized segments while verifyInventory() matches on the seed, moves and nethackrc triple, so the guard is weaker than the invariant its comment claims.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: the central premise is wrong. inventorySegment() at scripts/run-twoweapon-command.mjs:346-356 destructures only { seed, who, twoweapon, swap = false } and emits datetime: DATETIME, the module constant declared at :60; it does not thread datetime from the case, contrary to the finding's claim. The segment therefore carries no field a case can vary outside the match key, so whole-segment uniqueness is equivalent to match-key uniqueness rather than weaker than it. Do not reopen without a field that inventorySegment() threads from the case and the match key omits.

mutation.deltaRun: The audit-fix commit eb3a084 yields 0 sites: its js/ changes are comments in js/dothrow.js and js/cmd.js, and its production lines are unchanged. The window run's 7 mutants all sit in js/dothrow.js and scripts/dothrow.test.mjs killed all 7 in the first wave.

The whole of this range's eat.c work therefore carries no mutation evidence either way, which is why the pass was told to judge those lines by reading.
mutation.finderConclusion: The tests finder was given the empty survivor list and the reason it was empty, and it found what the mutation run structurally could not: four of the eight confirmed findings are assertions that cannot fail. The liquid-sound test asserted draws once after its last case while arena() clears the log between cases, so seven of eight cases -- both lava cases among them -- had their draw counts checked by nothing; every fixture in it gave the missile an owt equal to oc_weight * quan, so no assertion separated the ported weight() call from a read of the cached field; fprefx()'s cursed operands had no test at all, confirmed by a string mutant that left the suite green; and the hallucinating pear asserted its refusal without measuring the draws that decide whether the refusal fires before or after eat.c:2193's rn2. None of the four is an unmutated line; each is a weak oracle, which is the class of defect a mutation run cannot report.

readiness.boundary: The range runs from cmd.c rhack() receiving one of two keys to the message the command writes. Eating: `e` answered with the letter of an apple, a pear, or a give_feedback food, ending at the line fprefx() writes on the top line. Throwing: `f` at a quivered missile, ending at the Splash! or Plop! a landing in liquid sounds, or at the refusal that stands in for flooreffects(). passes.evidence: Counts: 13 raw, 12 deduplicated, 7 confirmed, 6 applied, 1 deferred, 5 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 8 mutants. Goal-closing pass for counted-command-occupation, covering both slices plus the tests deferral burn-down that ran alongside them, with the concurrency finder enabled because the occupation callback is asynchronous and set_occupation() stores a function on game state that a later turn invokes. The pass's most useful result is the second production defect: js/allmain.js interrupt_multi() carried a comment saying its refusal was a no-op because only a run reaches a positive multi, and this goal's own set_occupation() call falsified that in the same range. It is the second time a review has caught a refusal justified as unreachable becoming reachable when new code lands, after mattacku()'s AT_HUGS arm at d0612ef, and neither was visible to the development score. The first defect, a retried F-prefixed movement leaking context.forcefight into the next command, was confirmed with a wrong input; the fix agent traced the reachable one to mFL and measured it live. No score moved on any fix: 9/33 sessions, 1674/7765 screens, 125050/610816 random-number calls and 1685/7765 cursors before and after. Applied in 0fcfb88.

productionDefects.summary: js/cmd.js captureParsedCommand() and restoreParsedCommand() carried context.forcefight but not the DOMOVE_WALK bit cmd.c do_fight():1632 writes into gd.domove_attempting beside it. A retried command reached set_move_cmd() with an empty word, took its `!gd.domove_attempting && !u.dz` guard and became a rush, and rhack():3792's rush arm skips `svc.context.forcefight = 0`, so the flag outlived the command and turned the player's next movement into a force-fight nobody typed. The finding traced it to `FH`, which cannot reach the defect: only the eight do_move_<dir> rows carry CMD_gGF_PREFIX (cmd.c:2009-2023), so rhack():3693-3722 turns `FH` away. `mFL` reaches it, because was_m_prefix latches on do_reqmenu() and is never cleared (cmd.c:3771-3772), leaving CMD_M_PREFIX in force for do_run_east (cmd.c:2051). Driven live before the fix, a single-pass `mFL` ends with context.forcefight 0 and the same command retried past a hidden monster ends with 1.

js/allmain.js interrupt_multi() carried the claim that a run is the only way this port reaches a positive multi, so the arm that refuses allmain.c interrupt_multi():975-983's Norep(msg) half was a no-op. cmd.c rhack():3728-3729's set_occupation() call, landed by this goal, falsified it: a counted `s` or `.` leaves gm.multi above 0 with neither svc.context.run nor svc.context.travel set, which is exactly the state the guard admits, so a count spanning the turn the hero regains the last hit point or power point ends the segment where C prints one line and stops the count. The refusal itself is correct and fail-closed: it is taken ahead of nomul(0), which C runs first, so the interruption is wholly unapplied. Deferred rather than fixed because porting Norep(msg) makes js/regen.js regen_hp(), regen_pw() and js/allmain.js interrupt_multi() async and emits a message on a turn no input boundary bounds, which is new rendering behavior and needs a fresh recorded C case.

rejections.summary: state.go.occupation holds callbacks with two incompatible signatures, eatfood(state, env) and timed_occupation(state), and timed_occupation() drops the env js/allmain.js:1102 passes, so a timed occupation's handler can receive no injected operation.
rejections.counterEvidence: The facts hold and the impact does not. Enumerating extcmdlist[] prints exactly two rows carrying f_text, `115 search dosearch "searching"` and `46 wait donull "waiting"`, so timedOccupationFunction() can return only dosearch or donull. js/detect.js:844 dosearch(state, rawEnv = {}) hands dosearch0() a normalizeSearchEnv() that defaults every operation, and js/cmd.js:388 donull(state) takes no env at all; js/cmd.js:1528 already calls dosearch(state) with none from the typed path. Widening timed_occupation() to forward an env no reachable callee reads is the speculative plumbing AGENTS.md forbids, and it weakens the translation of C's argument-less `(*timed_occ_fn)()`. Do not reopen without a third f_text row in upstream extcmdlist[] whose handler reads an injected operation.

rejections.summary: js/mhitu.js could_seduce() refuses on the species half of C's disjunction alone, so an amorous demon's AD_PHYS claw stops the segment where C returns 0 and prints an ordinary hit or miss line, with no deferral recorded.
rejections.counterEvidence: Three independent refutations. Reachability: monsters.h:2922-2924 puts ATTK(AT_BITE, AD_SSEX, 0, 0) at slot 0 and the two AD_PHYS claws at slots 1 and 2, and mhitu.c mattacku()'s NATTK loop (766-800) resolves slot 0 first, where the hit side already stops at js/uhitm.js:1551 AD_SSEX and the miss side reaches could_seduce() with adtyp AD_SSEX, which the finding concedes is refused correctly; so the claws cannot be reached without an earlier stop. Causality: `git diff d0612ef..1842f5e -- js/mhitu.js` changes comment lines only and the species test at js/mhitu.js:143-144 is byte-identical across the range, so the narrowness is pre-existing rather than introduced. Resolution: mhitu.c hitmsg():43-69 has no AT_CLAW case and falls to `default: verb = "hits"`, so the proposed assertion on "The incubus claws you!" would fail against a correctly completed port. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

rejections.counterEvidence: Every production line the early stop crosses is exercised elsewhere. scripts/detect.test.mjs:398-411 drives the real secret-door find with multi 4 and asserts the event order ends at nomul(0) with multi 0 and context.run, travel, travel1 and mv all 0, which is nomul()'s `if (multi < nval) return` guard letting a positive multi through. scripts/detect.test.mjs:421-449 replays seed 8100006 with ten `s` presses through js/detect.js:410's own nomulZero injection, matching C's random-number calls, screens and cursors. scripts/count-prefix.test.mjs:180-206 pins moveloop_core() clearing go.occupation. The finding's own suggested validation is self-defeating: it states that removing the state.multi > 0 guard is already caught by the stub it criticises. rejections.summary: scanSession()'s keyCursor derivation and its relocated behavioral assignment have no test; scripts/scan-sessions.test.mjs only exercises the consumers, which receive keyCursor as a hand-written fixture field.
rejections.counterEvidence: The coverage gap is real and immaterial here. Both new rules are three lines mirroring helpers the same file's tests do pin: cursorState()'s read-the-preceding-step convention at scripts/scan-sessions.test.mjs:244-280 and again through commandsIssued() at :355-379, and isCommandRefusal() at :329. scan-sessions.mjs produces a human-read ranking report that no part of npm run checkpoint, the development score, or any generated-data check consumes, so a mislabelled row costs a reader's attention rather than game behavior. The proposed test also cannot be built as described: scan-sessions.mjs:82 and :109 fix DEVELOPMENT_DIR and accept no path, pinned by scripts/scan-sessions.test.mjs:53-59, so a synthetic session would have to be written into sessions/, which AGENTS.md forbids without explicit user approval. readiness.completeness: No unsupported behavior remains unstopped inside the boundary. Every reachable excluded branch refuses before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output: the count refusal calls resetCommandVars() and throws ahead of any dispatch, and interrupt_multi() throws ahead of C's leading nomul(0), leaving the interruption wholly unapplied. The one claim of unreachability this range falsified is that interrupt_multi() arm, now corrected in the comment and recorded as counted-occupation-full-health-interrupt; a sweep of the remaining unreachability claims in js/allmain.js and js/cmd.js found the rest still true.

passes.evidence: Counts: 33 raw, 29 deduplicated, 22 confirmed, 21 applied, 1 deferred, 7 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 8 survivors of 57 mutants. Two passes over one window, recorded as one entry because the second read the first's fixes. The first read 1842f5e3..a36313c and returned 18 raw, 17 deduplicated, 13 confirmed from five finders; its fixes landed in a634c32 and expanded scope into three C functions no finding named, which .agents/review.md makes a trigger for a full pass, so the second read a36313c..a634c32 and returned 15 raw, 12 deduplicated, 9 confirmed. That second pass is what justifies its cost: two of its nine were correctness defects the first could not have seen, because the fixes created them. One was a false reading of C, since parsebindings():7635-7641's failure arm does not return and txt2key('mouse1') answers M-o, so C reports an error and still binds key 0xEF where the port did neither. The other was a JavaScript hazard rather than a misreading: a bare property read on a prototype-bearing lookup made BIND=v:constructor a menu command, and the sweep it prompted found two more such reads in the status-highlight parser. The development score never moved anywhere in this window, at 9 of 33 sessions, 1674 of 7765 screens, 125050 of 610816 random-number values and 1685 of 7765 cursors at every commit, because no recorded session's rc carries a configuration error. That is why two passes rather than the score are the evidence here. Applied in a634c32, db6eda6, e8a88c2 and 3468c5a.

productionDefects.summary: js/options.js bind_key_matches() ported only cmd.c bind_key()'s match/FALSE arm, so the three config_error_add() calls C makes for a binding it accepts (cmd.c 2698, 2704, 2712) were unported and a BIND with a wrong parameter reported nothing. When such a BIND is an rc's only problem, config_error_done() returns 0, the port emits no raw-print screen and never reaches tty_wait_synch(), so the segment has one fewer input boundary than the recording and every later key and cursor is wrong.

js/options.js applyMenuBinding() still threw optionError() for parsebindings()'s Unknown key binding key, three lines above the sibling error the same range had converted, so half of one C function failed closed and half played on. BIND=zorkmid:redraw cost the whole segment above runSegment()'s catch.

js/options.js parseNethackrc() silently skipped a line with no ':' or '=', where cfgfiles.c parse_config_line() answers with a configuration error that a UNIX build never suppresses. It is one of the two commonest rc typos, and its absence under-counts the error summary whenever it coexists with a reported error.

js/options.js parseNethackrc() silently skipped a line whose statement name matches no CONFIG_STATEMENTS row, where cfgfiles.c parse_config_line():1436-1437 reports Unknown config statement. Reporting it today would wrongly flag WIZKIT, HILITE_STATUS, BOULDER and the rest, because the port's table holds 13 of config_line_stmt[]'s 31 non-syscnf_only rows.

js/options.js dropped cfgfiles.c's three remaining configuration errors in the section and CHOOSE arms, so a sectioned rc under-reported and under-counted: a player who writes [mysection] headers without a CHOOSE line gets one C error per header and none from the port.

js/options.js's three Missing parameter errors interpolated the raw comma element with its negation prefixes, where C's string_for_opt() reports the negation-stripped statement the function already held under another name.

js/cfgfiles.js gave the one C value configfile two JavaScript homes: get_configfile() read state.configfile while js/tutorial_startup.js read state.configFileName, each with its own '.nethackrc' literal, so whoever supplies the real path would set one and silently leave the other on the default.

js/tty_startup.js raised iflags.cbreak below its display guard, so a state without an nhDisplay kept the getret-only key set for the rest of the game. With cbreak falsy, xwaitforspace() accepts only CR and LF, so such a caller drains the input queue and dies as 'Input queue empty', which runSegment() mistakes for a deliberate end of recording.

js/options.js returned early for mouse1 and mouse2 on a false reading of C. In options.c parsebindings():7635-7641 only the accepting arm returns, and txt2key("mouse1") answers M-o, so C reports Error binding mouse button 1 and still binds key 0xEF where the port reported nothing and bound nothing.

js/options.js decided whether a name is a menu command with a bare property read on a prototype-bearing object, so inherited names such as constructor were treated as menu commands and appended verbatim to iflags.mapped_menu_op instead of reaching bind_key(). C compares against default_menu_cmd_info[] with strcmp, which holds no such name. The same unguarded read appeared at three further rc-text sites in the status-highlight parser.

mutation.finderConclusion: Composed from the window run over 1842f5e3..a36313c (37 mutants, 5 survivors) and the delta runs over the two audit-fix commits (18 mutants with 3 survivors, then 2 mutants with none). The tests finder read the survivors as pointing at real unpinned branches rather than at equivalent mutants: its findings on the bind path, the case-insensitive nothing spelling, and the tautological refused count all landed on lines the runs left alive. Patch 006 hooks nomux_putch() three times on process_text_window()'s path; both putchar hooks wrap the call in a curx-- compensation and the g_putch hook has none, while the loop pre-increments curx in its condition. So C records the stripped byte one column to the right of its own. A successor closing that entry by merging the two loops would have propagated a one-cell column error into every text and menu window instead of removing it, and screen comparison is per cell.

The same deferral omitted a second divergence in the same function: writeRecorderTtyWindowLine() writes a byte below 0x20 into a shadow cell that nomux_putch() discards, while writeStyledText() now drops it. The entry asks for the two loops to be merged, so without this the merge had no recorded statement of which behavior is right for control bytes.
